mr president, competition policy is an important instrument for the functioning of the internal market of the european union. the excessive concentration of economic and financial power in the hands of a few must be prevented. new objectives are often not achieved in practice because of oligopolistic and monopolistic actions. the annual losses due to the existence of cartels amount to between eur 181 and 320 billion, which is approximately 3% of the gdp of the european union. we urgently need to upgrade the existing legal framework to implement this important policy. state aid is a particularly sensitive issue: it must not be used illegally, anticompetitively or protectionistally. but when it comes to state support for peripheral regions and islands, flexibility needs to be increased. i welcome the decision to include social assistance for the transport of residents from remote regions in the general block exemption regulation. the same principle applies in croatia, where a pilot project of a helicopter emergency medical service was recently stopped despite a high number of interventions; unfortunately, about 30% of the croatian population does not have equal access to emergency medical care.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009 because i support the proposal of the european commission and the prompt implementation of international provisions in european legislation. i believe that it is necessary to ensure the recovery of tuna stocks, to set sustainable levels of catch, to limit fishing in certain areas and periods, and to establish clear rules for sport and recreational fishing. such as the conservation of biodiversity and marine ecosystems, which are severely threatened, so harmonized and strong rules certainly contribute to the effective protection of bluefin tuna.
written. ‒ the multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which is planned to be implemented by 2022 and was adopted in 2006, has so far produced positive results. all the activities undertaken to conserve bluefin tuna have resulted in a reduction in the risk of extinction of this species. by 2012, the bluefin tuna catch had been reduced by almost two thirds, which has had a positive impact on the recovery of the species and the balance of marine life. i supported the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean sea because of the fact that the activities undertaken so far have led to significant progress in the recovery process of the species. i consider that all the measures proposed relating to the recovery and monitoring of bluefin tuna are sound and feasible. the commission should be able to assess the impact of the measures on the marine environment and the marine ecosystems in the light of the scientific advice provided by the member states.
the proposal for a regulation on a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan ensures that the objective of the common fisheries policy, namely to regulate the use of living marine resources, is promoted, while ensuring that economic, social and environmental conditions are sustainable. it is necessary to emphasise that the union is part of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), which has the right to adopt decisions concerning the conservation and management of fisheries, making all decisions adopted binding. the purpose of this proposal is to implement into union legislation the measures adopted in the period 2012 to 2014 under the multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean adopted by iccat. the plan contains the regulation of technical measures that would help achieve the ultimate objective, measures such as the regulation of transport and the use of a stereoscopic camera to monitor the amount of catches. this proposal also introduces provisions empowering the commission to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i believe that protecting bluefin tuna can have a positive impact on the marine world, on the sustainability of the catch and on the recovery of the species in order to ensure the long-term economic exploitation of that species, to protect the fisheries and the fishermen who depend on the catch of bluefin tuna.
written. ‒ i support the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009. the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) has the power to take decisions related to the conservation of fisheries. these acts are binding and form part of eu law. in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan with the aim of restoring the species through a reduction in the tac. the plan introduces a gradual reduction of the allowable catch and measures related to the area and the period of the catch. the catch limit before the plan was around 33000 tonnes, which was gradually reduced to 12900 tonnes in 2012. the measure had a positive impact on the stock of the species and reached 13 400 tonnes in 2013. sustainable fishing is one of the fundamental principles we must uphold, while ensuring an equitable distribution of available quotas.

written. - i supported the proposal for a regulation on gas-fuelled appliances that would replace the current one and ensure the free movement of gas-fuelled appliances. i consider that this proposal will harmonise the conditions for the placing on the market of such appliances, which will contribute to simplifying environmental regulation and ensure a more favourable functioning of the market for appliances fuelled with gaseous fuels. i also support clear targets that will benefit both producers and consumers, taking into account safety measures and the rational distribution of energy. i consider that the proper and efficient functioning of the internal market requires common rules for gas appliances with regard to the health and safety risks arising from the use of gas and their energy efficiency. as the proposal is in line with the single market act which emphasises customer confidence in product quality as well as many improvements in addressing potential and possible problems, i voted in favour of its adoption.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the parliament and of the council on cableway installations because it harmonises the conditions for placing on the market of subsystems and safety components for cableway installations and guarantees the free movement of these products within the european union, which directly affects the single market. in order to achieve this, it is necessary to ensure a uniform implementation of the rules throughout the union, taking into account that certain aspects of cableways, such as regional planning and environmental protection, remain the competence of the member states. in addition, it is necessary to ensure legal clarity in order to implement the legislation in the area concerned in a consistent and effective manner.
written. ‒ i supported the report by mr antonio lopez-isturiz white because i believe that all the conditions for placing on the market of subsystems and safety components for cableway lines should be harmonised. member states shall take all necessary measures if it is established that an approved cableway installation could endanger the health, safety of persons and property, restrict the working conditions or prohibit its operation.
written. ‒ i support this proposal because i believe that member states should take all necessary steps to ensure that cableway installations can only be put into service if they comply with this regulation and if they cannot endanger the health or safety of persons or the safety of property, if they are properly installed and maintained and used in accordance with their intended purpose. i also support this proposal because it clearly states that when placing subsystems and safety components on the market, each importer of a subsystem or safety component should indicate its name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and the postal address at which it is available, as well as the websites if they exist. exceptions should be provided for in cases where the size or type of subsystem or safety component does not allow it. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the conditions for the granting of such rights. the penalties provided for should be effective, in accordance with the gravity of the offence. the commission should also be able to assess the impact of the proposed amendments on the environment and on the environment as a whole.
written. ‒ this proposal for a regulation on cableways aims at harmonising the conditions for placing on the market of subsystems and safety components of cableways in order to ensure their free movement in the internal market. it is commendable that the aim is to achieve maximum harmonisation in order to ensure simpler, better and safer rules. in that sense, it is better to have a regulation than a directive. the cableway is defined as elevator systems such as climbers, suspended cables, cab suspended cables, seats, towing cables and other cableway used for tourism or sporting purposes. it is positive that historical and museum traction installations and those with a forestry or agricultural function are not included in the regulation as the aim is to cover the safety aspects of public use, i.e. public transport use. i believe that the issue of safety, together with the importance of market surveillance and harmonisation, is crucial for this regulation and is dealt with in a qualitative way by the text of the proposal.
written. ‒ i agree with the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on cableways prepared by mr antonio lópez-istúriz white. the proposed regulation, which aims to update the existing wireline legislation in the european union, clarifies the inclusion of subsystems and safety components of cables in the scope of the regulation. one of the purposes of this proposal is to address the difficulties encountered in implementing directive 2000/9/ec. for example, authorities, notified bodies and manufacturers have entirely different answers to the question whether a specific type of installation is covered by directive 2000/9/ec and therefore has to be manufactured and certified in accordance with the requirements and procedures of the directive. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measure is imputable to the state. i therefore consider this proposal to be of great importance and i fully support it.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, but this explanation of vote is a criticism of the existing system of evaluating the work of meps in the european parliament solely on the basis of the statistical number of parliamentary activities promoted in croatia, which does not actually reflect the actual quality and quantity of work, efficiency and above all the success of the representative action.
written. ‒ i support the proposal for a cable car regulation which is an example of harmonised legislation within the eu. the purpose of the proposal is to harmonise the conditions under which subsystems and safety components for cables are placed on the market and to ensure the free movement of these products within the union. all safety components and subsystems will have to meet the standards prescribed by the regulation. the regulation will replace directive 2000/9/ec of 20 march 2000 relating to cableway installations for the carriage of persons. the change of the applicable legal instrument, i.e. the replacement of a directive by a regulation, seeks to ensure better regulation and simplify the regulatory framework. the regulation will avoid unnecessary transport costs and will set out clear and detailed rules applicable throughout the union. the regulation will also reduce the risk of divergent transposition, i.e. ensure a uniform level of security protection throughout the union, and prevent deviations in the internal market.
written. ‒ i supported the amendments to the legislation on cable cars because the new legislative framework brings standardised obligations to manufacturers, importers and market surveillance authorities, which will lead to a significant reduction in administrative barriers, as well as a clearer regulatory environment for all economic operators. in addition, i consider the conformity assessment procedure, i.e. the selection of a random sample and the examination of all its subsystems or safety components, to be an appropriate and objective way of determining whether a sample will be accepted or rejected. in particular, i support efforts to allow the use of alternative technical solutions, as well as to place cableways of historic construction outside the scope of this regulation and under the jurisdiction of national legislation. i also support the decision that member states should continue to have the responsibility to regulate other aspects of cableways such as land use, spatial planning and environmental protection.
written. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the commission delegated regulation of 25 november 2015 amending annex iii to regulation (eu) no 978/2012 of the parliament and of the council applying a scheme of generalised tariff preferences because it is a motion for a resolution by a political group that clearly had no chance of winning the support of parliament and i therefore decided to follow the alde group's position and voted against the resolution.
written. ‒ customs preferences are provided for by a special agreement on incentives for sustainable development and good governance, provided that it has ratified all the necessary conventions and that the latest available conclusions of the supervisory authorities do not indicate serious deficiencies in the effective implementation of any of those conventions. whereas the supervisory authorities of the relevant conventions have identified significant deficiencies in a number of conventions relevant to the tso+ and that those problems represent a serious deficiency in the effective implementation of the relevant conventions listed in annex viii to the tso regulation; i supported the objection because the granting of customs benefits requires a case-by-case assessment to meet all the necessary conditions due to the fact that customs benefits are not granted automatically.

written. ‒ taking into account the situation in kyrgyzstan, i support the resolution on these regulations concerning the application of the gsp. according to the reports of various committees, the human rights situation in the kyrgyz republic is of concern and the government of the kyrgyz republic has not fulfilled its obligations towards the un and other international organisations and committees with regard to the report on compliance with certain standards, which is a prerequisite for the country to become a beneficiary of the gsp scheme. in particular, we are talking about reports that warn of the widespread practice of torture, the lack of basic legal protection, political and police repression, ethnic discrimination, and the widespread occurrence of the most serious forms of violation of children's rights, such as sexual exploitation, the abduction of minors, physical abuse, etc. also alarming is kyrgyzstan's proposed law on homosexual propaganda, which violates an individual's right to privacy as well as freedom of expression. the european union must promote good governance, human rights and democratic principles and insist on respect for these values in its relations with third countries and partners.

written. ‒ the main objective of the gsp is to facilitate preferential access to the eu market for developing countries and territories by reducing customs duties on their products. the customs preferences on the eu market should allow developing countries to participate more in international trade, generating additional export revenues that they can then use to implement their policies of sustainable development and poverty reduction and diversify their economies. the general system of preferences does not require or expect these countries to grant reciprocal preferential access to their markets. for the reasons stated above, i voted against this objection to the delegated act on the gsp scheme.
written. ‒ i support the objection to the delegated act on the gsp, as kyrgyzstan has not met the agreed requirements. the european union grants preferential customs treatment to certain countries. in the case at hand, the european union has authorised kyrgyzstan to place certain goods on the union market under preferential customs conditions, but kyrgyzstan has not complied with the union's requirements. we therefore need to suspend this process until kyrgyzstan meets the eu's conditions.
written. ‒ i voted against the objection to the delegated act on the system of generalised tariff preferences, initiated by the club of european united left - nordic green left meps, because they consider that kyrgyzstan is not making progress in implementing the provisions of the convention against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. i consider that the objection does not take into account the positive steps of the government of kyrgyzstan as one of the poorest countries in the region. the government of the kyrgyz republic has taken positive steps to improve human rights by various initiatives to combat violence against women, improving the refugee law, introducing human rights education programmes for public officials and judges, striving to guarantee the independence of judges, and directly applying international treaties before courts. in addition, i believe that the gsp is an additional motivation for kyrgyzstan to continue reforms, as well as to strengthen its economy, increase exports and promote industrialization, and therefore should not be abolished.
written. ‒ the commission simply re-writes the 1996 regulation which allows baby food to contain up to 30% sugar and i therefore support this objection. in 2015, the world health organization recommended that sugar and salt should not be added to food for babies under two years of age. introducing high-sugar foods, especially at such an early stage, can contribute to a higher number of obese children and affect the development of taste preferences that are still developing in children.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the commission delegated regulation supplementing regulation (eu) no 609/2013 as regards specific ingredient and information requirements for processed cereal-based foods and baby foods as it objects to the commission delegated regulation. the protection of infants and young children should be the primary objective of the delegated regulation, but the maximum sugar level is too high and the zero tolerance for pesticides does not apply in full. poor nutrition is one of the leading causes of disease and death worldwide, and i believe that when it comes to infant nutrition, special care should be taken and the highest standards used. on the other hand, public confidence in the eu institutions and the transparency of the decision-making process must also be increased.
written. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution because poor diet is by far the biggest cause of illness and death worldwide, even greater than tobacco, alcohol and physical inactivity combined. the commission has not submitted to parliament and the council the report on food for young children required by regulation (eu) no 609/2013 (article 12) and which is a necessary condition for national strategies to reduce childhood obesity. the maximum level of sugars should be significantly reduced in accordance with the who recommendations.
written. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on a delegated regulation supplementing regulation (eu) of the european parliament and of the council with regard to specific ingredient and information requirements for processed cereal-based foods and baby foods objecting to the commission delegated regulation. i believe that in accordance with the precautionary principle in infant formula, there should be no untested and emerging technologies, such as gmos and nanotechnology, whose long-term dangers are not yet known. in view of the sensitivity of infants and the possible impact of pesticides on their endocrine system, i consider it necessary to introduce a zero tolerance to pesticides in baby food. i also agree with the experts of the world health organization that for the first six months of a child's life, the best food is mother's milk. the inability to breastfeed is unfortunately a disorder that young mothers are increasingly suffering from, due to stress, unfavourable working conditions, in part, and as a consequence of insufficient social care in some countries with a poor legislative framework on maternity leave, but it is not a rule and a reason to avoid highlighting this important recommendation of the world health organization. for these reasons i supported this resolution and i expect the new commission proposal to take parliament's objection into account.
written. ‒ i support the objection to the commission delegated regulation allowing a higher level of sugar in baby food (30% of the energy value, i.e. 7,5 g sugar/100 kcal) than recommended by the world health organisation. such a solution would jeopardise the healthy development of children, i.e. eating foods with these sugar levels at an early age may contribute to the growing obesity of children and the development of unhealthy habits, which is of particular concern given that poor diet is the leading underlying cause of disease worldwide. scientific research and findings on the safe use of breast-milk substitutes should also be taken into account and it should be ensured that the appropriate age of consumption is emphasised in the labelling of the product. this is, among other things, the duty of the union as an international organisation that leads in promoting high-quality public health principles. unfortunately, in croatia too, the regulation on processed cereal-based foods and baby foods for infants and young children allows a level of up to 7.5 g of sugar per 100 kcal and i hope that this provision will soon be changed.

mr president, madam high representative, following the terrorist attacks in paris last year, the french minister of defence invoked for the first time in history article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union and asked all member states for 'all the help and support in their power' in the wake of an 'armed attack on french territory'. many misinterpret this part of the lisbon treaty as a sort of pendant to article 5 of the north atlantic treaty, which, in the event of an attack on one member, obliges all the others to come to its aid. the european partners can practically not refuse the french request because it would not be solidarity. and many did. it is true that france can be helped in many ways and that support need not be military. but even more acutely, many questions about the internal security of the european union go beyond the protection of national states. the best response would be for the common security and defence policy to cease being the weakest link in european integration. the proposal for a common defence force first came to light in 2014, when we heard that the european union could save between €21 billion and €60 billion by increasing the synergy of defence policies and introducing a common defence system. however, the development of a common security and defence policy very often raises more questions than it answers. perhaps it is appropriate to start from the fact that it is not unified even among the general administrations of the european commission.

‒ in 1979, the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution was concluded with the aim of limiting and preventing air pollution in order to prevent negative effects on people and the environment. already, it was proved that air pollutants can travel up to several thousand kilometers before being deposited. in 1998, the convention was extended to include the protocol on heavy metals and the protocol on persistent organic pollutants. the heavy metals protocol obliges signatory states to monitor emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury, to phase out leaded petrol and to reduce the level of mercury in alkaline batteries. the protocol on persistent organic pollutants allows for the reduction or elimination of persistent pollutants and the regulation of pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs), dioxins, furans and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. the amendment to the heavy metals protocol explicitly sets stricter emission limit values for dust (particulate matter dispersed in the gaseous phase) and monitoring of emission values for lead, cadmium and mercury on an annual basis. i supported the european parliament resolution on the amendment of the heavy metals protocol. i therefore also supported the amendment of the protocol on persistent organic pollutants, as it reports annually on emissions of polychlorinated biphenyls (pcbs), confirming that emissions are lower than in the reference year and creating new limit values for dioxins and furans.
‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution is designed to protect the environment from air pollution. several studies conducted between 1972 and 1977 showed that air pollutants can travel several thousand miles before settling. therefore, the problems caused by air pollution should be addressed at the international level. the convention is the first international legally binding instrument in this field. the convention has created a framework for controlling and reducing the adverse health and environmental impacts of transboundary air pollution. the amendment of the protocol is already largely covered by eu legislation, but the new directive will establish updated national emission ceilings for certain air pollutants and provide the conditions for annual national emission inventories covering emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury. as indicated, the amendment is fully in line with existing eu legislation and ratification of the amendment will be a step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution.

written. ‒ i supported the recommendation of mep la vie to amend the 1998 heavy metals protocol to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, which was the first international legally binding instrument in this area when it was signed in 1979. since its entry into force in 1983, the convention has been extended to include eight protocols identifying concrete measures to be taken by parties to reduce their emissions of pollutants. the 1998 amendment to the protocol has been largely incorporated into eu legislation. the new directive sets national emission ceilings for certain air pollutants and provides for annual national emission inventories which should cover, inter alia, emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury.
written. ‒ i supported the proposed amendment of the 1998 aarhus protocol on persistent organic pollutants to the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, intended to protect the environment from air pollution. the european union already has this area in its legal acquis, regulated by the ambient air quality and clean air for europe directives, but also by the industrial emissions directive and a package of other related regulations, which constitutes a coherent package that tightly controls environmental pollution by persistent organic pollutants in the european union. it is those rules that ensure that operators of large stationary emission sources use best available techniques (bat), that waste incinerators operate in accordance with the prescribed emission limit values and take effective measures to control those emissions from mobile sources, and that persistent organic pollutants are transported and disposed of in a prescribed manner once they become waste. i am pleased that conventions and protocols as international law mechanisms follow eu policy and allow further progress to be made in the fight for a cleaner and healthier planet at global level. the adoption of the amendments to the protocol is an important step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution by persistent organic pollutants. in this regard, i once again welcome the legislative resolution that has just been adopted.
written. ‒ i support the amendments to the 1998 protocol on persistent organic pollutants to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. it is a protocol to an important convention, which was the first international legally binding instrument in this field of protection. the amendments to the protocol include seven new substances, changes to the rules on implementation and on the restriction of certain emissions, and the inclusion of polychlorinated biphenyl. the ratification of these amendments will ensure a higher level of protection of the environment and human health from organic pollutants. the act on the implementation of regulation (ec) no 850/2004 on persistent organic pollutants in croatia allows for the direct application of these rules. i hope that its implementation will also ensure the protection of human health and the environment in the croatian border areas around slavonski brod, which are exposed to cross-border pollution.
written. i agree with the recommendation of my colleague giovanni la vie on the draft council decision on the acceptance of the amendments to the 1998 protocol on persistent organic pollutants to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution. this convention is the first legally binding convention of its kind and entered into force in 1983. it is intended to protect the environment from air pollution and to create a framework for controlling and reducing damage to human health and the environment caused by long-range transboundary air pollution. the amended 1998 protocol is already largely covered by eu law and will be further transposed through a revision of the directive on national emission ceilings for certain pollutants. the amended protocol also sets out (1) stricter dust emission limit values for certain major stationary sources and (2) flexible transitional arrangements that will be beneficial for those member states that will accede to the amended protocol before the end of 2019, including countries in eastern and south-eastern europe.
‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution is designed to protect the environment from air pollution. several studies conducted between 1972 and 1977 showed that air pollutants can travel several thousand miles before settling. therefore, the problems caused by air pollution should be addressed at the international level. the convention is the first international legally binding instrument in this field. the convention has created a framework for controlling and reducing the adverse health and environmental impacts of transboundary air pollution. the amendment of the protocol is already largely covered by eu legislation, but the new directive will establish updated national emission ceilings for individual air pollutants and provide conditions for annual national emission inventories covering emissions of pops, including pahs, pcdd/pcdfs, hcbs and pcbs. as indicated, the amendment is fully in line with existing eu legislation and ratification of the amendment will be a step towards a higher level of protection of human health and the environment from transboundary air pollution.
written. ‒ i supported the amendment of the protocol on persistent organic pollutants because the amendments are fully in line with european union legislation and the updated emission limits for certain atmospheric pollutants will provide tools to address and monitor progress in emission control. the amendment to the protocol will improve the monitoring and help reduce or eliminate releases, emissions and spills of persistent organic pollutants. i believe that the amendments will ultimately lead to a reduction in air pollution and its harmful effects on human health and the environment with a particular focus on long-range transboundary air pollution.

written. - two years after the signing, the marrakesh treaty has still not been ratified. despite the support of the european parliament, the commission and the vast majority of member states, several large eu member states oppose ratification and block the council's compromise. this delay in ratification means that today 250 million blind and partially sighted people, as well as others who are unable to use standard printing, are still unable to have equal access to books, information and published works as other people do. this undermines almost every right guaranteed by the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, from education to information to political participation. access to culture and information is a fundamental human right, and the marrakesh treaty is the first step in realising these rights. however, without ratification, it's all in the words. the delay was caused by a lack of political will, not legal obstacles. it is time for the eu to bridge the gap between words and deeds and to fulfil its obligations towards people with disabilities. the european union and all member states should set an example for their citizens in integrating people with disabilities into society and in making their daily lives easier, rather than more complicated. i therefore fully support the ratification of the marrakesh treaty and appeal to all institutions to do so as soon as possible.

written. ‒ gender equality is one of the eu's core values, as enshrined in the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights, and the eu is committed to mainstreaming it in all its activities. gender equality is also a strategic objective that is key to achieving the overall europe 2020 objectives of growth, employment and social inclusion. the european parliament, in its resolution of 9 june 2015, clearly called for a new, separate strategy on gender equality and women's rights for the period after 2015. the need for a new strategy is best illustrated by the results of the public consultation, which showed that 90% of respondents supported the new strategy. i therefore support calls on the commission to adopt immediately, in response to the results of the public consultation and the views of parliament and the council, a communication on a new strategy for gender equality and women's rights for the period 2016-2020, addressing gender equality issues in the areas of violence against women, working time, decision-making, health, education, media and external relations and in line with the international agenda. i also agree with the call on the commission to propose legislative initiatives in its work programme to eliminate the remaining inequalities between women and men in the eu, which is why i supported this resolution.
written. ‒ gender equality is one of the european union's founding values. unfortunately, there has been a lack of perseverance in the fight for equal rights for women and men. women today still face traditional prejudices that affect the division of labor in the home, educational attainment, the workplace, and society as a whole. exposure to discrimination is the biggest problem. the prevailing social perception is that women have difficulty competing with men in certain types of jobs, especially in the scientific and technological fields, which makes them pre-select completely different occupations and very rarely enter entrepreneurial waters. in addition, they face difficulties in reconciling work and family life, problems with unequal pay, and underrepresentation in politics and the economy that could affect collective decision-making. for all these reasons, and aware of the magnitude of the problem, i supported a european parliament resolution aimed at eradicating discrimination, respecting the dignity of women, the right to equality in the labour market and raising awareness of prejudice and the traditional division of roles.
the european parliament, in its resolution of 9 june 2015, clearly called for the adoption of a new strategy on women's rights and gender equality for the period after 2015, given that the objectives set out in the previous strategy (2010-2015) had not been met and that it was not sufficiently comprehensive to contribute to greater gender equality. in 2014, almost one third of women (32,2%) worked part-time, and according to eurostat data, the employment rate of men in 2014 in the member states of the european union remains higher than the employment rate of women (70,1% compared to 59,6%). over the past decade, there has been a slowdown in policy action and reforms at the european union level to strengthen women's rights and gender equality. the right to equal treatment is one of the fundamental rights of european society. i do not support the motion for a resolution because i believe that the existing legislation must be put to better use.

on behalf of the alde club. mr president, i would like to thank first of all president mikhailova and all colleagues from other groups for accepting this initiative. i have devoted my entire political career to strengthening the local and regional self-government units. stronger cities, stronger municipalities, stronger regions have always meant a stronger quality of life for me. what i want to emphasize today is that i am 100% convinced that the principle of subsidiarity has no alternative. we really need to implement the principle of subsidiarity to the full, because it is a well-known european practice that the most decentralised countries, such as denmark, have by far the best standard, the best development. i think the most centralized countries, like my country croatia or like greece, have big problems in development, and there's something going on that's crucial. the key is the absorption power. we have a common situation today that it is precisely the super-centralized states that do not have a quality absorption power. that is why i am all for the possibility of direct access by cities and regions to european funds, because we often have political competition between national authorities or some regional or local authorities. in this way, if we have the possibility of direct access by local and regional authorities to european funds and various other sources of funding at european level, i am sure that we will strengthen the quality and security of life in many cities and in many regions of the european union. i add to this the need for good cross-border cooperation, for good cross-border cooperation financing, where we have excellent experiences, for example ipa adriatico is a fantastic good experience of good cross-border cooperation financing and of course macro-regional cooperation. i conclude with the conviction that it is through this issue that the commission will be more sensitive to local and regional development.
madam president, local and regional authorities are best placed to deal with the problems faced by different environments. and that is why i think they should have a greater role in the management of structural and investment funds. but i am afraid that in some member states such bodies do not have the necessary capacity or experience to manage such programmes. larger and more developed member states, which have for decades been committed to the principle of decentralisation and to strengthening the capacity of local and regional self-government, have a major advantage in this respect over smaller, newer and less developed member states. i therefore believe that the commission should encourage member states to decentralise and exchange best practices in the area of local and regional self-government structures, with the aim of having as many decisions as possible in the foreseeable future that are important for the lives of citizens taken in their immediate vicinity.
madam president, madam commissioner, first of all i would like to thank my colleagues on the committee on regional development for raising this very important issue. every investment from every fund ends up in some local or regional environment and that's why their participation is important. i therefore agree with and support the proposals of my colleagues that local and regional authorities have direct access to european funds or that rules be set by which central authorities will be obliged to allow local and regional authorities to participate in these funds on equal terms without partisan discrimination and without regional discrimination, which sometimes happens. i also invite the commission to propose measures to enable this mechanism to be monitored. with that i am convinced that the use of european funds would be much better than it is now.
madam president, what i would like to stress is that the fundamental principles of regional policy are partnership and multi-level governance. however, they are often not applied in practice. we have the opportunity to see in many member states operational programmes which are adopted at national level and in which local and regional units are not recognised. that is why i propose that in the future, when we think about the development of cohesion policy, one of the rules we should introduce is that operational programmes are really adopted regionally, that they are regional operational programmes and that ownership of their implementation is at the regional level. what is very important is the inclusion of regional units in economic policies, this is often neglected. we talk about the need to link cohesion policy with the european semester, but without the role of the regional units we cannot even achieve that.
written. because of their proximity to citizens, local and regional authorities play a key role in shaping and implementing eu strategies. local and regional authorities can create new jobs, stimulate entrepreneurial innovation and growth through the eu's cohesion policy. regional and local authorities need to make more efforts to achieve a higher rate of use of the european structural and investment funds. it is therefore essential to address the structural weaknesses of local and regional authorities in the design and implementation of operational programmes in order to give these bodies a better position in cohesion policy. cohesion policy is a good example of multitier governance with a 'bottom-up' approach. in this approach, local and regional authorities in their management of the european structural and investment funds strike a balance between achieving greater economic, social and territorial cohesion and the impact of european union policies at local and regional level. local and regional authorities today face challenges such as globalisation, climate change, energy security and migration flows, and it should be borne in mind that each region has its own specificities and specific needs.

vice-president of the commission. – madam president, it is very clear from the discussion we are having here that the smuggling of tobacco products is something that concerns us all. it affects our public health, our public finances and the quality of our law enforcement. the interest of parliament is shared by the commission. this is an important priority in our work. today we are debating it because the eu’s first anti—fraud agreement with the largest tobacco manufacturer in europe, philip morris international (pmi), is set to expire in july. we are currently reflecting on the way forward and we are benefiting from the debate in this chamber. yesterday we disclosed the commission assessment of the agreement. it is the result of very thorough discussions with the member states and all relevant services. we wanted to make sure that it was as good as it could be, and we acted on our promise to parliament that we would engage all the services of the commission, and in particular the directorate—general responsible for health, to produce this assessment. we did that. let me start by recalling why we have this agreement in the first place. in the past, significant volumes of contraband cigarettes from the major tobacco manufacturers were being smuggled illegally in the eu. we pushed the companies to take action, and the very extensive investigation by olaf led to litigation by the eu and its member states before the us courts against several tobacco manufacturers, resulting in anti-fraud agreements. under these agreements, the manufacturers accepted regulatory discipline that, at that time, was very innovative, included global tracking and tracing of their products, due diligence and know-your-customer, as well as anti-money-laundering provisions. they also offered financial incentives to these companies to comply with the agreements. what is the assessment telling us? first, even if we cannot make – as has been pointed out – direct causality between the agreement and the results in terms of the reduction of smuggling, we have achieved the key objective. the seizure of pmi contraband notified by member states under the agreement was reduced by 85% between 2006 and 2014. that is a fact. second, the agreement provided national and european investigators with intelligence that has led to many seizures, arrests and criminal indictments. transnational criminal organisations were dismantled and illegal factories in some member states were closed down. third, it must also be made clear that the reduction of the pmi contraband did not lead to the overall reduction of the eu tobacco black market. the assessment is very clear about that. what we shrank has been taken over by the so—called ‘cheap whites’. fourthly, the total payments asked by us – annual and seizures – made by the four manufacturers into the eu have so far surpassed eur 1.1 billion, including around eur 100 million in seizure payments. fifth, lessons have been learned from the implementation of these agreements, especially in terms of global tracking and tracing, and these lessons are now very valuably integrated at international level. today, the growing problem of cheap whites requires us to continue to work with our member states to tackle it. i am very pleased to report that olaf has taken this mission of tackling illegal smuggling very seriously, together with member states. last year, 2015, 600 million cigarettes were confiscated, and a vast share of those were cheap whites. as has been stated, we have new tools today. the world has changed. we have the tobacco products directive from 2014 which focuses on production and sales into the european union. the track and trace features under this directive will become mandatory for all manufacturers and importers in may 2019. just as importantly, we have the who framework convention on tobacco control. it requires 40 ratifications to enter into force. so far we have 15. i look forward to parliament voting in may on ratification by the eu, and i can tell you that we are putting a lot of attention and energy into facilitating more ratification so we can have it in force by 2022. so what is the future of the pmi agreement? we are clear that our overarching goal to fight the illicit tobacco trade remains, and we have to make sure we are as effective as possible. we are strengthening our capacity for that. in march this year we will have an independent laboratory to help us in this fight. we are very keen for the regime that is put in place in the eu and internationally to be active and to deliver in this fight. now the question is whether or not, between today and the time when we have the directive in place, 2019, or the time when we have the protocol enacted in 2022, we still need a legally-binding instrument to fight illegal trade. this is what i am here to listen to. i will take this debate into account so we can make an informed decision in the commission in the weeks to come.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft council decision authorising the republic of austria to sign and ratify the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters and the republic of malta to accede to that convention in the interest of the european union, as the european parliament thereby expresses its consent. i consider that the convention is of particular importance in the field of cross-border supply of documents and that it is in the interest of the union and the member states concerned to strengthen the single regime for the supply of documents in cross-border relations with third countries. it is also important to emphasise the role of the union in that process which authorises member states to act on its behalf in order to accede to the convention. accordingly, and given that the said convention is already applied by 25 eu member states, i support the willingness of austria and malta to accede to it.
written. ‒ the 1965 hague convention established a system defining how each signatory state may transmit judicial and extrajudicial documents abroad in civil or commercial proceedings. the convention does not concern the work of international organisations and the eu has to vote on the participation of each member state in the convention. at present, 26 of the 28 member states are party to the convention, and now austria and malta have expressed their wish to sign the convention. i supported the accession of austria and malta to the hague convention as the convention has proven to be a practical tool for the settlement of judicial and extrajudicial disputes in practice so far. it is in the interest of the eu that all member states are in one system for the cross-border supply of documents to third countries.
written. ‒ i welcome the decision of austria and malta to accede to the hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. austria and malta are the only two member states of the european union which have not yet acceded to the said convention, and their accession will allow the member states to act on behalf of the union, as the eu as an international organisation cannot accede to the convention. i therefore invite parliament to support the accession of austria and malta to the hague convention and express the hope that this accession will be another in a series of steps taken by the member states to strengthen the union's position in its relations with third countries.
‒ the convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters is a multilateral agreement signed at the hague on 15 november 1965. the convention provides channels for the transmission of judicial or extrajudicial documents sent by one member state of the convention to another member state of the latter. in other words, the convention provides one formal channel for transmission, via the central body of the requested state, and several alternative channels for transmission. the hague conference currently has 80 members: 79 member states and 1 regional economic community organisation. in total, 26 eu member states are applying the convention. given that the hague convention has proved its usefulness in the field of cross-border service of documents, as evidenced by the number of acceding states to the convention, it is in the interest of the union as a whole that all member states accept one regime for the service of documents in cross-border relations with third countries. therefore, i support the accession of the last two member states, austria and malta, to the hague convention on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters.
‒ the 1965 hague convention provides for the channels of transmission to be used when judicial or extrajudicial documents need to be transmitted from one contracting party to another. however, it is important to note that the convention only covers cross-border supply of documents to or from third countries, and 26 of the 28 member states already apply the convention. austria and malta, as the two remaining member states, have expressed their wish to accede to the convention, and the eu must authorise the member state in question to act on its own behalf and accede to the convention. malta has already deposited its instrument of accession, but has made a declaration that its accession will not take effect until this decision is accepted. austria is also awaiting this decision in order to be able to carry out the formalities for acceding to the said convention. the hague convention has proven its usefulness in the field of cross-border supply of documents and it is in the interest of the eu as a whole as well as of the two member states concerned to have one regime for the supply of documents in cross-border relations with third countries and therefore austria and malta should be allowed to accede to the 1965 hague convention without hindrance.

written. ‒ since 1995, there has been a convention to protect, in accordance with criminal law, the financial interests of the eu and its taxpayers. eu countries must introduce effective, proportionate and dissuasive criminal sanctions for fraud affecting the eu's financial interests. the convention and its protocols are open to all countries acceding to the eu. given that croatia joined the eu on 1 july 2013 and thus acquired the status of full member, i welcome croatia's accession to the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests with a view to increasing transparency in the use of public funds, both at european and national level.

written. ‒ the treaty of accession of the republic of croatia of 2011 introduced a simplified system for the accession of croatia to the conventions (and protocols) concluded by member states on the basis of article 34 teu (former article k.3 teu). article 3 (4) and (5) of the act provides for the accession of croatia to those conventions and protocols on the basis of the act of accession. article 3 (5) of the act of accession provides that the council is to adopt a decision to that end in order to determine the date of entry into force of those conventions for croatia and to adapt the conventions for the accession of the new member states (which would certainly include the adoption of the conventions in the croatian language so that those versions could be 'equally authentic'). the commission recommends that the council adopt a decision to determine the date of entry into force of those conventions for croatia, and i therefore support the report.
written. ‒ a simplified system of accession to conventions and protocols previously concluded by member states was made possible for the republic of croatia by the treaty of accession to the eu of 2011. article 3 (5) of the act of accession provides that the council is to determine the date of entry into force of the conventions and the adaptation of those conventions for croatia. this includes publishing conventions in croatian. parliament accepted the commission's view that no further adjustments are necessary to bring croatia into line with the convention of 26 july 1995 on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, but that it is only necessary to determine when that convention will enter into force in croatia. i therefore accept and approve this report and the commission's recommendation.
written. ‒ it is a legal standard in modern democracies to provide criminal protection for public budgetary funds, i.e. to qualify their misappropriation in a certain amount as a criminal offence. the most important eu legal instrument in the field of criminal law protection of its budgetary resources is certainly the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests. as a member of the interclub for integrity transparency, anti-corruption and organised crime, i am pleased that croatia has formally acceded to the convention, which is the backbone of the obligations of member states with regard to the protection against fraud, corruption, money laundering or the criminality of legal persons, which also damage or jeopardise budgetary resources. although, like most member states, croatian legislation provides for specific criminal offences to protect the expenditure and revenue of the eu budget and all offences relevant to fraud against the eu are prescribed by criminal law, i welcome this commission recommendation on croatia's formal accession to the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests, as this is the only way to finally put us all together against all those who see the budget as a means of their personal enrichment.

written. ‒ freedom of movement is one of the four fundamental freedoms on which the eu is founded. the freedom of citizens, including croats, to work anywhere in the eu is a key aspect of eu citizenship and includes the right of croatian citizens to seek employment in another eu country, to work there without the need for a work permit, to reside there for that purpose with their family members and to enjoy equal treatment with citizens in terms of access to employment, working conditions and all other social and tax benefits. the aim of this regulation is to make the eures network an effective instrument for jobseekers or employers involved in labour mobility within the eu. this would create a pool of job vacancies and jobseekers whose profile could be consulted by anyone at eu level. given that high unemployment is affecting some parts of europe, including croatia, whose unemployment rate is 18.5%, which is 8% above the eu unemployment rate, i support this regulation as it contributes to improving labour mobility within the eu, creating new opportunities for employing workers and helping employers to fill vacancies more quickly and efficiently.
‒ 1.1 million european citizens cross the border for work every day, and in 2013 more than 7 million eu citizens lived and worked in another member state, 78% of whom were economically active and 68% of whom had a job. such mobility is made possible by the fact that eu citizens can move freely, seeking work in another member state without a work permit. despite the fact that the number of people living in a member state where they were not born has increased by 60% since 2005, this number still represents only 3,1% of the total eu workforce. the eu has 25 million unemployed, of which more than 5 million are young people, but there is still a shortage of skilled workers in many regions of the member states. to facilitate and simplify the employment of eu citizens in other member states, the eures network was launched in 1993, allowing for the free movement of workers within the member states and to switzerland, norway, iceland and liechtenstein. such a network provides free information on life and work in individual member states and connects employers with jobseekers, but its reform is needed to adapt it to the new conditions and situation in the eu in economic and social terms. i therefore support the report.

written. ‒ i support the decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund under the 2016 eu general budget, at the request of belgium, to provide assistance to redundant workers in the glass sector. the belgian region of wallonia, and in particular the area of the cities of namur and hainaut, is known for its tradition of glass production, which employs a considerable number of workers in the region. this industry sector was in serious crisis, both due to the global financial crisis and the fact that most of the european market was taken over by foreign producers. unfortunately, the price of the crisis and globalization this time is paid by the workers of wallonia, 412 of them. i believe that this measure will make it easier for the dismissed workers to find another job, start their own business or retrain, which will also help to reduce the unemployment rate in wallonia. i therefore call on parliament to respond to the request of belgium and to approve this decision.
the european globalisation adjustment fund was created to provide additional assistance to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows due to globalisation, such as the closure of large companies or the relocation of production outside the eu, or as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. for the period 2014-2020, the fund has a maximum annual budget of eur 150 million and can finance up to 60% of the cost of projects designed to help redundant workers find new employment or set up their own business. the strong historical tradition of glassmaking in wallonia is facing major challenges today, including overcapacity in asia combined with higher production costs and stricter environmental standards in europe, which ultimately resulted in the dismissal of 412 belgian workers from hainaut-hamur glass who had become surplus. for this reason, i support this measure, which provides eur 1 095 544, which will benefit 412 former workers and up to 100 targeted young people not in employment, education or training, to provide them with integrated training and facilitate their job search.

written. ‒ the commission's growth survey report for this year focused on three main areas: investment, structural reforms and fiscal responsibility. i believe it is important that this report should lead to a thorough debate at european level on three important issues: the question of deepening coordination at euro area level, the future direction of the eu's fiscal, monetary and structural policies, and the question of democratising the decision-making process on the recommendations of the european semester. i agree with the rapporteur that it is essential for europe to find responsible solutions to the new challenges it faces, above all the threat of terrorist attacks and the migrant crisis, in order to assert its political legitimacy. i believe that parliament's support for this report makes a significant contribution to the definition of the priorities of the european semester for economic policy coordination in 2016 and sends an important message to all actors to actively engage in the european semester so that we can all together drive a stronger economic recovery of the european economy.
written. ‒ the annual growth survey identifies what more can be done at eu level to help member states boost growth, enhance economic convergence, create jobs and strengthen social justice. the importance of an integrated approach to economic policy based on three main areas of action that must work together is therefore underlined: stimulating investment, accelerating structural reforms and implementing responsible, growth-friendly fiscal consolidation. only by working together can confidence be restored and the eu as a whole be brought back to growth, and this requires a strong commitment from member states to act at national level. for this reason, i welcome the 2016 annual growth survey package and the proposed policy mix of investment, structural reform and fiscal responsibility, which aims to promote higher growth rates and strengthen european recovery and upward convergence. i would like to stress that, given the slowdown in the world economy, the eu cannot rely on exports but needs to increase domestic demand to increase the potential for growth. for this reason, private and public investment needs to be increased. surplus countries should expand their budgets to support investment, while deficit countries should be allowed more fiscal space through flexibility to allocate more to investment and structural reforms.
written. ‒ the eu is emerging from a long economic crisis that has caused serious social hardship and undermined the potential for economic growth. at the same time, the eu is facing new challenges, in particular the threat of terrorist attacks, geopolitical instability in its neighbourhood and an unprecedented number of asylum seekers. it is important that the eu develops the means to address these challenges in order to ensure its political legitimacy in this situation. it is equally important to boost economic recovery and create quality jobs. in addition to the economic challenges that have arisen in the midst of the digital revolution and technological innovation, it is also important to look at longer-term challenges such as climate change, robotization, demographic change and the shift towards a multipolar world. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the establishment of a european data protection supervisor. all the structural reforms that will result must reflect and be based on the experiences of the past and the challenges that lie ahead. although the concept of structural reforms is generally understood to involve reducing the role of the state in the economy, thus creating more flexible markets, such an approach has not always led to improved productivity, but has even increased inequalities and deflationary pressures. i therefore support the report.

madam president, in the last 100 years, the production of garbage has increased tenfold. a significant part of it ends up in the sea, posing a serious threat to ecosystems and human health. marine litter is the result of exclusively human activities - it knows no borders and is a persistent problem that extends far beyond the source of pollution. that's why i want to talk about the problem of marine litter in the coastal area of croatia. it is found in large quantities on beaches and on the seabed, and is carried by currents and winds from the neighbouring adriatic countries. waste collection is mainly carried out on the initiative of local communities and associations, as recently in the town of trstenik. in addition to the environmental cost, marine litter has a socio-economic impact as it affects coastal communities, as clean coastlines are key to tourism. although this is not enough, it is worth praising the marelit and defishgear projects. the objective is for countries to work together to tackle marine litter more effectively in order to achieve together the important goal of good ecological status for all marine waters by 2020.

written. - according to recent research, animals are becoming more resistant to antibiotics and diseases are spreading among them. the report suggests implementing measures to reduce the spread of diseases, especially those that are transmissible to humans. i supported this report because it defines the rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases which are transmissible to animals or humans.
written. ‒ i welcome the adoption of this regulation, which represents a significant step forward in the implementation of the action plan against the increased threat of antimicrobial resistance. the regulation lays down measures to collect relevant, comparable and sufficiently detailed data on the use of antimicrobial medicinal products in animals in the member states. those measures aimed at the prudent use of antimicrobials allow this act to emphasise the link between animal welfare and public health. prevention measures increase the quality of life of farmed animals, reduce the need for the use of those products and their reduced use allows for a longer period of safe use of antimicrobials until resistant strains of bacteria emerge. this also reduces the impact of antimicrobial resistance on people, as they are less exposed to antibiotic residues in food and to the persistence of antibiotic stocks in human medicine. it is in this public health interest of this regulation to focus on the quality of life of both humans and animals. the impact is also not negligible for the globally recognised safety and high quality of european food products, which results in a comparative advantage of european agriculture on third markets.
written. ‒ animal health law affects all animals in the eu, both domestic and wild, that can be affected by infectious diseases. in addition to the animals affected, this act also affects between 20 and 30 million people in the eu who are involved in working with animals. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the principle of non-discrimination in the case of the use of animals for the purpose of animal health protection. accordingly, the responsible and prudent use of veterinary medicinal products and antibiotics in animals should be necessary and mandatory. for that reason, i support this bill which establishes a clear and transparent way to implement disease control measures to ultimately ensure that pain, misery and suffering are avoided when disease control measures are implemented.
written. ‒ i supported this proposal for a regulation as it focuses on the prevention of diseases that can have deadly consequences for animals and humans in the member states of the union and beyond. animal diseases such as avian or swine influenza are a threat to the economy, food safety and public health and therefore require comprehensive protection for animals and humans. the proposed regulation introduces a thorough categorisation of diseases, clarifies the definitions of responsibility for animals and their condition, and prioritises biosecurity, i.e. vaccination instead of shot, and the separation of sick animals from the rest of the animals and of new animals from old ones. in order to monitor the implementation of this regulation, member states should collect relevant, comparable and sufficiently detailed data on the use of antimicrobials in animals and submit those data to the commission in order to ensure the safe use of those products and to reduce the risk of antimicrobial resistance. the reports to be published by the commission on the basis of these data will help to further develop preventive measures against animal diseases in the eu member states.
written. ‒ this regulation lays down rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases transmissible to animals or humans, but it does not contain provisions specifically governing animal welfare, although animal health and welfare are linked. the union has a well-developed animal welfare legal framework covering different species (such as laying hens, laying hens, pigs, calves) or activities (such as farming, transport, slaughter, research, etc.). this animal welfare legislation will necessarily continue to apply. the commission fully supports the full attention to animal welfare in accordance with article 13 of the treaty and within the limits set thereby, including the full implementation and appropriate development of that legislation, and i therefore voted against the rejection of the council's position at first reading.
written. ‒ i voted against the proposal to reject the council's position and the proposal to bring together and update the different parts of european legislation in the field of animal health by means of a new law. in particular, many member states have mandatory systems for the identification and registration of pet animals, but i consider that there are differences between the types of data stored, the registrations and the management levels at which those data are stored. i believe that proper conditions for the identification and registration of dogs and cats would reduce the scope for document forgery and illegal trade. i also consider that the low vaccination rate of animals increases the risk of antimicrobial resistance in pets, which is an additional risk factor for the development and transmission of antimicrobial resistance in humans. i also support the establishment of a computerised database for dogs and cats to ensure effective disease control measures and to facilitate the movement of animals between member states of the european union, and therefore do not support the rejection of this proposal.

written. ‒ gender-sensitive policy means including a gender perspective in all aspects of eu policy, i.e. in the preparation, design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, in legal measures and in consumption programmes, in order to achieve equality between women and men. it is not an end in itself but a key means of achieving gender equality, always in combination with other concrete measures and policies aimed at promoting gender equality. since 1996, the commission has been committed to a two-pronged approach to achieving gender equality. this approach includes the integration of a gender perspective into all policies and the implementation of specific measures to eliminate, prevent or eliminate gender inequalities. since the ep adopted a resolution on gender equality in 2003, each parliamentary committee appoints one of its members as gender equality officer. however, in order to reduce the under-representation of women in key decision-making positions at political and administrative level, gender equality needs to be implemented equally at staff level. i therefore welcome the conclusions of the resolution and the emphasis on the need for gender-sensitive amendments, gender impact assessments and gender budgeting to include a gender perspective at all levels, in all areas and at all policy stages.

written. ‒ council directive 1999/32/ec has been substantially amended several times and, following an agreement between the european parliament, the council and the commission, a codification procedure has been required. the basic version of the directive itself seeks to reduce emissions of sulphur dioxide from the combustion of certain types of liquid fuels and thus to reduce the harmful effects of such emissions on humans and the environment. the directive sets maximum permitted sulphur content of heavy fuel oil, gas oil, marine gas oil and marine diesel oil used in the union. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to amend the list of substances which are subject to the restriction of the sulphur content of heavy fuel oil. the consolidated directive should, after the implementation of the codification, be in line with the revised appendix vi to the international convention for the prevention of pollution from ships as amended by the protocol of 1978 and containing provisions for the prevention of air pollution from ships. the amended annex vi to the protocol entered into force on 1 july 2010, so that in order to provide greater legal certainty to the obligors in the implementation of the obligations of the convention in the territory of the union, i support this codification.
written. ‒ the european commission directive 1999/32 on the reduction of sulphur in certain liquid fuels aims to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions from the combustion of certain liquid fuels, thereby reducing the harmful impact of such emissions on humans and the environment. those reductions in sulphur dioxide emissions will be achieved by imposing a limit on the sulphur content of the combustion of certain liquid fuels, which creates a condition for their use in the territory of the member states. sulphur dioxide emissions are one of the causes of acidification and particulate matter in the european union, they cause acid rain that pollutes forests, rivers, lakes and other natural resources, and they are one of the factors causing damage to ecosystems, biodiversity and human health. for this reason, i support the consolidation text of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels.

the european union and andorra signed on 12 february 2016 an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information to promote international tax cooperation and the enforcement of tax obligations at international level. the agreement is an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and is an upgrade of the 2004 agreement, which guarantees that andorra applies measures equivalent to those in the eu directive on taxation of savings income on interest. the european union and andorra shall cooperate with each other in the exchange of information on the financial accounts held by the citizens of the other party in accordance with the provisions of the agreement. the aim is to tackle situations where taxpayers want to conceal capital representing income or assets that have not been taxed, and therefore supported the report itself.
written. ‒ in order to enhance international cooperation and compliance, the european union and the principality of andorra signed on 12 february 2016 an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. the contract is an important step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. the commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the rules for the application of this article. this agreement will also help andorra, which has recently introduced changes to its tax system such as taxing the personal income of citizens of the principality. the purpose of this treaty is to enable the resolution of situations of misconduct in which a taxable person seeks to conceal capital, income or assets which have not been taxed in another country. i support this treaty because it represents a major step forward in the fight against tax fraud by allowing for the immediate exchange of account information held by eu citizens in andorra and vice versa. the agreement will allow for the proper and unambiguous identification of taxpayers, the assessment of the likelihood of tax evasion and the enforcement of tax laws in cross-border situations.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement between the european community and the principality of andorra on the taxation of savings income on interest, as i consider it to be an upgrade of the 2004 agreement and an important step in the fight against tax fraud and evasion. the agreement will ensure that the financial accounting system of andorra is in compliance with the requirements of the financial accounting standards board (fasb) and the financial supervisory oversight and audit authority (fsa) as set out in the annex to this agreement. i am of the opinion that this agreement will address situations where taxpayers seek to conceal capital representing income or assets not taxed. i also believe that the taxpayers involved will be identified precisely and unequivocally, the likelihood of tax evasion will be assessed and unnecessary further investigations will be avoided.
