written. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the new alliance for food security (2015/2277 ((ini)) as, in addition to all the positive assumptions contained in the new alliance for food security, this document also identifies problems that should be addressed. in particular, the new alliance for food security in africa, launched in 2012 under the auspices of the g8 as a major public-private partnership to boost private investment in agriculture to improve food and nutrition in sub-saharan africa, aims to support poverty reduction efforts, provide food security, assist local and family farms and should become a true instrument of sustainable development and an instrument for providing assistance to sub-saharan africa. the problem is that large multinational companies operating under the new alliance favour large-scale contract farming, which puts small producers in a subordinate position. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the aid granted to the beneficiary was granted in breach of the rules on state aid. small producers need to be put in a better position.
‒ the new alliance for food security in africa was launched in 2012 as a major public-private partnership to boost private investment in agriculture to improve food security in sub-saharan africa. instead of supporting the new alliance's modern agricultural model, based on large-scale industrial agriculture, more should be invested in family farms. family farmers and smallholders are the main investors in african agriculture and provide over 60% of employment in africa. the eu must play a key role in transforming the new alliance into a real instrument, and this requires addressing governance and property rights, promoting sustainable family farming, access to land and security of tenure. the eu should not use oda to support transnational corporations that act as monopolies or cartels and thus contribute to undermining the local private sector. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the new regulation to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. i supported this report because it would benefit family farmers the most and ensure that consumers have access to quality food at affordable prices.
the new alliance for food security in africa (nafsn) was launched in 2012 under the auspices of the g8 as a public-private partnership (ppp) aimed at attracting private investment in agriculture to improve food and nutrition security in sub-saharan africa. the european union's experience in successfully implementing a common agricultural policy based on small farms is a valuable knowledge and experience to be shared with developing countries to ensure that they too have sufficient supply of quality food for their populations. i believe that agricultural investment policies in africa should be targeted to support the development of the local economy, including small producers and family farms. i welcome the commitment to promote inclusive growth based on agriculture and supporting smallholder farming and helping to reduce poverty, hunger and malnutrition. in addition, it is important to call on african governments to invest in local food systems to improve rural economies, ensure decent jobs, equitable social protection networks and labour rights, and improve conditions for democratic control of access to resources. i supported this resolution because helping that part of the world depends not only on money and donations but also on caring for their self-sustaining, inclusive and sustainable economic growth that starts in the agricultural sector.
‒ the new alliance for food security in africa aims to improve food security by helping 50 million people in sub-saharan africa to escape poverty by 2020. given that over the past 30 years in africa, investment in smallholder farming has been neglected and low-income countries have become significantly more dependent on food imports, making them vulnerable to price fluctuations in international markets, i call on governments and donors to suspend or review all policies, projects and advisory activities that directly encourage and facilitate the competition for arable land through highly unfair projects and investments or that indirectly encourage increased pressure on land and natural resources and that can cause serious human rights violations, and i call for support to be provided for policies that protect the needs of smallholder farmers, in particular women, and promote sustainable land use. i also encourage eu member states to seek to transform the new alliance into an instrument of sustainable development and an instrument to support family farming and local economies in sub-saharan africa, and recall that family farmers and smallholders produce approximately 80% of the world's food and are responsible for more than 60% of employment in sub-saharan africa.
written. ‒ i supported the report by mep marie heubuch on the new alliance for food security in africa. in order to improve food and nutrition security in sub-saharan africa, private investment in agriculture needs to be increased. the new alliance, launched in 2012, includes the g8 members, the african union, the new partnership for africa's development (nepad) and the comprehensive african agricultural development programme (caadp). one in four people in sub-saharan africa is malnourished. as the world's leading humanitarian donor, the european union has an important role to play in transforming the new alliance into an effective mechanism for providing financial and operational assistance to local economies and family farmers in sub-saharan africa. effective implementation of international standards will help reduce poverty levels and increase food security in the region.
written. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa seeks to improve food security and nutrition so that 50 million people in sub-saharan africa can be lifted out of poverty by 2020. this proposal is of great importance as family farms and small farmers are the main investors in african agriculture. investment in small farms has been neglected, and this has increased dependence on food imports. i believe that we need to develop resilience to excessive food imports and encourage organic production and diversification of food at local level. i also think that the proposal is very important because it is predicted that by 2050 about 70% of the world's population will live in cities and it is intended to open up the possibility of better jobs in rural areas as well. in view of the future volatility of international markets and the need for all countries to avoid the risk of over-dependence on imports and to encourage investment in domestic production, i supported the proposal for a new alliance for food security.
written. ‒ with 50 million people in sub-saharan africa living in poverty, i believe that the new alliance can improve food security and help them. the parties have agreed on a framework for cooperation among states setting out commitments to facilitate private investment in the agricultural sector in africa. following the 2008 food crisis, there was a global recognition of the need to support small farmers producing food for domestic markets. in view of the above, i support this report on the new alliance for food security. also, in africa, over the past 30 years, investment in small farms has been neglected, and food imports by low-income countries have increased significantly. in developing countries, food security depends greatly on the sustainable use of natural resources. the commission has also identified a number of other areas where the union should be able to contribute to the development of the food sector. finally, given that it's predicted that 70 percent of the world's population will be living in cities by 2050, i think the food question will require a response at both the local and global levels.
written. ‒ the new alliance for food security in africa is conceived as a large-scale public-private partnership aimed at boosting private investment in agriculture to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa. in drawing up the framework for cooperation, the states have hardly consulted smallholders, although they should be the ultimate beneficiaries of the new covenant. the european union and the member states have a key role to play in transforming the new alliance into a real instrument for supporting family farming and local economies in sub-saharan africa in order to tackle poverty and food and nutrition insecurity. the main private participants in the new alliance are multinational companies that already benefit from a dominant market position and are often granted business, customs and tax benefits in host countries. i support the motion for a resolution because i believe that the european union should suspend its current support for the new alliance, as its ability to contribute to poverty reduction and food security is seriously called into question. the commission should also be able to provide support to the member states in the form of grants, loans and guarantees.
‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa was launched in 2012 under the auspices of the g8 as a major public-private partnership aimed at boosting private investment in agriculture to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa. the alliance aims to involve private partners in investing in african agriculture and to establish a framework to facilitate private investment. however, it is questionable how much exceptionally large public-private partnerships such as the new alliance can contribute to poverty reduction and food security, as it is the poorest communities that are at risk of taking on the burden of social and environmental risks. i therefore believe that the european union and its member states should suspend their current support for the new alliance and instead invest in a sustainable model of agriculture to ensure that consumers have quality food at affordable prices, and i abstained.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the evaluation of international accounting standards and the activities of the international financial reporting standards foundation, the european financial reporting advisory group and the public interest oversight committee because i believe that without harmonisation there is neither a single nor a competitive market. the european union's framework for the regulation and supervision of financial services should be based on consistent and harmonised international standards in view of the development of the single market for capital and in order to make the european union a world market leader. it is also necessary to take into account the public interest in all companies listed on the stock exchange being treated equally and to ensure reliable information on the creditworthiness of companies.
written. ‒ ifrs standards change in line with dynamic changes in the environment such as uneven economic and financial developments, the volatility of financial markets and institutions. depending on the environment, standards are also updated or discontinued. the ias together with international auditing standards (isas) constitute a key component for the efficient functioning of the capital market and the internal market. the main purpose of the ifrs is to enhance accountability by working to reduce the information gap between firms and investors, to improve international comparability and the quality of financial data, and to introduce greater transparency. in order to facilitate the movement of global capital, a single global system of accounting standards is needed to harmonise the different standards. in the european union, long-term investors and various stakeholders have already raised the issue of the inconsistency of international accounting standards with the legal requirements set out in the accounting directive on several occasions. the most common discrepancies are in the principles of governance and prudence, which hamper global capital flows. the need arises to define and develop harmonised financial reporting standards and to ensure consistency and coherence. in view of all the above, i have endorsed this report.
written. ‒ international accounting standards have been introduced to increase the efficiency of the european capital market by increasing the transparency and comparability of financial statements. today, these standards are used by individuals and businesses in over a hundred countries to prepare their financial statements. the european commission has assessed how the application of the standard has fulfilled their task of creating a common accounting language. however, the report notes that there is still room for improvement in the way they are harmonized internationally, simplified, and made more understandable and consistent. i welcome the expressed desire to make further progress in standardising accounting rules and to address the shortcomings identified, and given the exceptional importance of standards in removing obstacles to new investment and in developing the single capital market in the union in general, i support this report. however, i would invite the commission to check whether the existing accounting standards allow for any tax fraud.
written. ‒ the purpose of international financial reporting standards is to enhance accountability by reducing the information gap between investors and firms, to protect investments and to introduce transparency by improving the international comparability and quality of financial data, and to enable investors and other market participants to make informed economic decisions and thereby influence the behaviour of participants in financial markets and contribute to the stability of those markets. the financial statements are of particular importance for the protection of shareholders, members and third parties and such types of undertakings do not provide guarantees to third parties in excess of the amount of their net assets. in the light of the above, it is appropriate to note that the accounting model of 'decision making utility' is not fully consistent with the accounting function of 'capital adequacy' as described in the case law of the court of justice of the european union and in the accounting directive, which leads to the conclusion that the conceptual basis of the accounting framework for international financial reporting standards does not cover the purpose of financial statements in eu law for which the same standard of accuracy and presentation of the specified figures applies, as set out in lord hill's reply e-016071/2015 of 25 february 2016, as a holistic assessment of the significance of individual figures and qualitative explanations is required to achieve the principles of accuracy and presentation of figures.
written. ‒ the report by mr stoloyan highlights the importance of accounting standards in the development of the single capital market in the member states, especially in the context of capital markets that will help further strengthen european influence in the world. the adoption of international financial reporting standards ensures their alignment with the interests of the european economy. i supported the report by mr stoloyan which welcomes the evaluation of international accounting standards carried out by the commission but also reminds the commission that it is necessary to present the legal changes needed to address the deficiencies and non-compliances identified by the evaluation.
written. ‒ i supported this report, but this explanation of the vote arises as a criticism of the existing system of evaluating the work of meps in the european parliament solely on the basis of the statistical number of parliamentary activities promoted in croatia, which does not actually reflect the actual quality and quantity of work, efficiency and above all the success of the representative action.
written. ‒ the threat to economic and financial stability and the decline in public confidence in the social market economy model arise as a consequence of the distorted presentation of company accounting data. i support this report because international accounting standards and international auditing standards are one of the key components necessary for the effective functioning of the capital market and the internal market. it is also important to note that reducing the information gap between investors and firms and enabling investors, but also other market participants, to make informed economic decisions are among the aims and purposes of the international accounting standard. furthermore, a global system of accounting standards is essential for global capital movements. finally, i think this report is important because it also puts the emphasis on strengthening europe's position to ensure that the principles are embedded in the whole standard-setting process and in the recognition of standards.
written. ‒ international accounting standards are an important part of the eu framework for the regulation and supervision of financial services. accounting standards are of great importance in the development of the single capital market in the european union, in particular in the context of the capital markets union project. the application of international financial reporting standards in the eu has contributed to strengthening the single market and has also strengthened the competitiveness of the european economy by enabling companies to attract capital and investments in global capital markets. international accounting standards must be approved before they become part of union legislation, thus ensuring that they are in the interest of the european economy. i support this resolution because i believe that the adherence to and application of financial reporting standards must be ensured in order to guarantee a level playing field for all in the single market.
written. ‒ i supported the report on the evaluation of international accounting standards and the activities of the international financial reporting standards foundation, the european financial reporting advisory group and the public interest oversight committee. i consider that internationally accepted accounting standards are necessary in a globalised world and that, in interaction with other financial services regulation legislation, they form an important part of the union framework for the regulation and supervision of financial services. i would also like to stress the importance of the role of accounting standards in the development of the single capital market in the european union, especially in the context of the capital markets union project. i believe that the application of international financial reporting standards in the european union contributes to strengthening the single market and to enhancing the competitiveness of the european economy.
written. ‒ i support this report which deals with the issue of european cooperation within the framework of the un operational peace initiative. this initiative comes with recommendations for the eu to improve its engagement in africa in the field of peace support operations. the european union has a mandate to help africa ensure its own security.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on peace support operations eu cooperation with the united nations and the african union (2015/2275(ini)) as peace support operations are one of the ways of responding to crisis situations with the support of internationally recognised organisations such as the un or the african union, with the aim of preventing armed conflict, preserving or building peace, respecting peace agreements and resolving emergencies in some countries. the aim of peace support activities is to contribute to the creation of a stable, secure and more prosperous environment in the long term. a coordinated external action is needed, using diplomatic, security and development instruments. the report welcomes the un-au strategic partnership for peacebuilding and crisis management and its priorities for the period 2015-2018 and the importance of making further efforts in conflict prevention. member states should not act in isolation in support of peace support operations. it is called for european action to be prioritised to help manage the borders whose permeability is one of the causes of the rise in terrorism.
written. ‒ an inefficient institutional structure has led to frequent unrest and crises, and recently the security situation in africa has deteriorated significantly. the emergence of rebel groups, mercenaries and terrorism has shaken the entire african union, alarming the un's role as an internationally recognized ambassador for peace. un peacekeeping missions and counterterrorism actions are becoming increasingly common practice in many areas. the number of unstable states and areas without organized security has increased significantly, reflecting the increasing poverty of the population, violence and corruption in the african region. the eu is a key partner of the un in its efforts to reduce crises, with four military operations and five civilian missions coordinated with un missions. the objective of the mission is to ensure lasting peace, to create a secure, prosperous and stable environment resulting in adequate protection of civilians, respect for fundamental human rights and economic development of the african union countries. the main mechanism for european cooperation with the african union is the african peace facility, established in 2004 with a budget of eur 1.9 billion. i supported the report on peace support operations eu cooperation with the united nations and the african union, as strengthening institutional capacity is of key importance to the african union.
written. ‒ the un currently has nine peacekeeping operations in africa, and peace support operations are an important response to crises and war situations and can contribute in the long term to the final cessation of long-standing wars and conflicts. peace is the security of the whole world. the key to the success of peacekeeping operations in this deteriorating international environment, which significantly affects the natural and operational needs of an operation, is to approach each crisis individually and to offer a comprehensive response. the eu's cooperation with the un and the african union in peace support operations is crucial. this cooperation can be achieved through the exchange of resources, information, technology, training programmes and logistical support. the eu also has its own instruments through the common foreign and security policy with which it can intervene and contribute to peace in crisis countries. africa is a crisis hotspot that is never extinguished, the conflicts on the african continent involve hundreds of different interest groups and extremist groups of people who are difficult to reconcile, who are plotting the fate of ordinary people whose lives are at stake. in africa, development and progress have been halted. the obstacles to africa's future are crises and wars, and peace is a necessary precondition. i therefore supported this resolution which will involve the eu more closely in cooperation with the un and the au in establishing and maintaining peace.
written. ‒ peace support operations are one of the ways in which crisis responses are provided with the support of internationally recognised organisations such as the un or the african union, under a un mandate, for the purpose of preventing armed conflict, restoring, preserving or building peace, respecting peace agreements and addressing complex emergencies and challenges arising in failing or weak states, given that the stability of the african and european neighbourhood would significantly benefit all countries. the objective of the peace support operation is to contribute to the creation of a stable, secure and more prosperous environment in the long term, as good governance, justice, strengthening the rule of law, protection of civilians, respect for human rights and security are essential prerequisites for achieving this objective, with successful reconciliation, reconstruction and economic development programmes contributing to the achievement of self-sustaining peace and prosperity. i support the peace support operation in cooperation with the united nations and the african union, given that the security situation in africa has changed dramatically over the last decade, with the emergence of terrorist and insurgent groups in somalia, nigeria and the sahel and saharan countries, and that peacekeeping and counter-terrorism operations have become the rule rather than the exception in many areas. more and more unstable states and regions are without organized government, leaving many exposed to poverty, lawlessness, corruption, and violence.
‒ the european union has invested some €1.5 billion in africa over the past two decades to support demining and help mine victims, making it the largest donor in the region. i supported the report by mr van orden with the aim of increasing the emphasis on political, humanitarian and development efforts to support civilian peacekeeping operations and to provide support to military actors. the report expresses particular concern at the high number of cases of sexual exploitation and forced prostitution of women, child prostitution and trafficking of children. it calls for respect for human rights, the avoidance of all forms of violence and reiterates that human rights must be at the heart of any initiative undertaken in the framework of peace support operations.

written. ‒ given that the creation of a more prosperous, secure and stable environment in the long term, as well as respect for human rights, protection of civilians, strengthening of the rule of law are among the primary objectives of peace support operations, i support this report. unfortunately, peacekeeping and counterterrorism operations have become the norm rather than the exception in many areas due to the emergence of terrorist and insurgent groups in africa over the past decade. the eu is currently engaged in four military operations and five civilian missions in africa, often operating in parallel or sequential with un operations, reflecting the eu's contribution to strengthening the african peace and security architecture. i also believe that one of the ways to respond to crises is to support peacekeeping operations. moreover, more than 120 000 personnel are deployed in 16 un peacekeeping operations and the un is also a major force for international peace and security. finally, i believe there is a clear need for mutual support in security and development interventions.
written. ‒ peace support operations are one of the ways in which crisis responses are provided with the support of internationally recognised organisations under the united nations mandate for the purpose of preventing armed conflict. the objective of peace support operations is to contribute to the creation of a stable, secure and more prosperous environment, for which good governance, justice, protection of civilians, respect for human rights are essential preconditions. in the last decade, the security situation in africa has changed dramatically. terrorist and insurgent groups have emerged in somalia, nigeria and the sahel and saharan countries, and peacekeeping and counter-terrorism operations are becoming the rule rather than the exception. there are more and more areas without organized government, as well as unstable states. such a situation results in poverty, lawlessness, corruption, and violence. the development of a trilateral partnership between the un, the eu and the african union is a key factor in preventing further conflict. i support the guidelines set out in the report because i believe that there is an urgent need to invest more effort in conflict prevention in order to improve the security situation in africa. i think that other factors, such as political or religious radicalization, displacement, and climate change, need to be considered.
written. ‒ as peacekeeping operations are one of the ways in which crisis responses are provided with the support of internationally recognised organisations such as the united nations or the african union, i supported the report which seeks to increase the european union's contribution to peacekeeping operations and cooperation with the united nations and the african union. i consider that the objective of peace support operations is to contribute to the creation of a stable, secure and more prosperous environment in the long term, and the basic prerequisites for achieving that objective are good governance, justice, the rule of law, the protection of civilians, respect for human rights and security. i would point out that european countries contribute greatly to the united nations system by providing financial support for un programmes and projects and i call for further efforts to be made to strengthen international security, stability and peace.
written. ‒ the food supply chain is a key sector for the daily lives of consumers and for the economy as a whole. the sector employs more than 47 million people within the eu and accounts for 7% of eu gdp. the eu has so far had measures that were mostly voluntary and that have proved insufficient. as many as 95 percent of the players in the food supply chain have been victims of unfair trading practices. it is precisely because of the perishability of food products that purchasers of goods very often manipulate contracts with suppliers. primary producers are faced with the choice of either letting their product rot or selling it for a pittance.
written. ‒ i voted for the report on unfair trade practices in the food supply chain (2015/2065(ini)) as it is a serious problem where this report does not solve the problem but certainly contributes to a better understanding of the difficulties faced by small food producers and can contribute to possible solutions. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the exporting producer concerned has been able to obtain a benefit from the scheme. it is necessary to ensure that european competition law takes account of the specificities of agriculture and that this is in the interests of producers and consumers. conditions must be created for a more efficient market that will allow consumers to access products at competitive prices and protect primary producers. european legislation exists in terms of tackling unfair practices towards consumers and in terms of market competition, but there is no legislation dealing with unfair trading practices between different actors in the food supply chain. small farmers are the foundation of food production. it is a huge sector that employs a huge number of people, provides livelihoods for many families and enables development in rural areas. food production is a strategic resource and cannot be left entirely to market regulation.
written. ‒ the prevalence of unfair trading practices is becoming a serious problem, present in an increasing number of economic sectors. the latest commission report confirmed that unfair practices can occur in all parts of the food supply chain. the importance of the food supply chain in the european union is reflected in the number of employees, which exceeds 47 million and accounts for 7% of gross value added. the most common forms of unfair trading practices used by operators in the food supply chain are restrictions on market access, sudden and unjustified termination of contracts, delays in payment, insufficient or ambiguous information on the terms of contracts, charging for services that are fictitious, forced participation in promotional rebates and charging for better product positioning in markets and other additional unfair fees. unfair trading practices can have a negative impact on individual actors in the food supply chain, most often micro, small and medium-sized agricultural enterprises, spilling over to other sectors and the eu economy as a whole. the commission should be able to assess the impact of unfair practices on the union industry, in particular on the union industry's ability to compete in the global market, and to take appropriate measures to address the identified unfair practices. i supported the report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain. i believe that european competition law should give consumers access to a wide range of quality products at competitive prices.
written. ‒ data in croatia show that in the last few years almost 100 000 family farms have disappeared from the register and their fate is unknown, food imports are increasing and the purchase prices of agricultural products are falling. milk buyers are breaking contracts with producers overnight without any consequences, and in one year, 2,000 milk producers in croatia have gone out of business, while most of them still have loans and their existence and the future of their children are in question. similar examples are not lacking in other eu member states. in order to put an end to unfair trading practices in the food supply chain in the countries of the western part of the eu, a certain level of voluntary relations has been established between the partners in the chain, and on the initiative of the producer and purchaser organisations. however, despite good intentions and a desire to regulate the relationship voluntarily, such a system does not work either. i therefore believe that it is necessary to adopt framework legislation at eu level to tackle the problem of unfair trading practices and to guarantee fair conditions for european farmers and consumers to buy and sell. this is what the agri amendments were called for and adopted, and this report has sent a clear message that we will no longer tolerate unfair trading practices.
written. ‒ given that producers sometimes trade at a loss after negotiating with other actors in the food chain, e.g. in cases of devaluation and price cuts in supermarkets, and that unfair trading practices are an obstacle to the development and proper functioning of the internal market and seriously impede the proper functioning of the market, the european parliament welcomes the steps taken so far by the commission to combat unfair trading practices in order to ensure a more balanced market and to overcome the current fragmentation resulting from different national approaches to tackling the problem of unfair trading practices in the eu. however, it points out that these steps are not sufficient to tackle unfair trading practices. i welcome parliament's decision to crack down on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain and believe that the strengthening and establishment of producer organisations should be accompanied by an increase in the bargaining power of farmers in the food supply chain, in particular by enabling them to collectively negotiate contracts.
written. ‒ unfair trading practices are present in large numbers and in many economic sectors and can occur at any part of the food supply chain in business-to-business transactions. cross-border trade between member states accounts for 20% of total eu food and drink production and employs more than 47 million eu citizens. the commission should be able to assess the impact of the measures on the financial markets and to take appropriate measures to address the potential impact of unfair trading practices on the financial markets. i supported the report by the czech representative to introduce consistent and stringent measures to prevent such problems in the eu food supply chain and to make markets more efficient with a level playing field for all partners.
written. ‒ i supported this report, but this explanation of the vote arises as a criticism of the existing system of evaluating the work of meps in the european parliament solely on the basis of the statistical number of parliamentary activities promoted in croatia, which does not actually reflect the actual quality and quantity of work, efficiency and above all the success of the representative action.
written. ‒ the size and strategic importance of the food supply chain for the european union should be taken into account, as this sector employs more than 47 million people in the eu and the total value of the eu market for products related to the retail food trade is estimated at eur 1.05 billion. i support this report as unfair trading practices in the food supply chain are difficult to interpret as a breach of the current competition law, as its existing tools are only effective in the case of some forms of non-competitive behaviour. in this connection, i consider that unfair trading practices are a serious problem that exists in many economic sectors. the same problem has negative effects on the weakest link in the food supply chain and has been highlighted by the commission, the european economic and social committee and the parliament on several occasions. food trade has an increasingly important cross-border dimension and operators in the food supply chain benefit greatly from the single market. finally, small, medium and micro-enterprises, which account for more than 90% of the european economic structure, are particularly vulnerable to the effects of unfair trading practices, and competition law only partially covers the same inequalities in the food supply chain.
written. ‒ generally speaking, unfair trading practices can be defined as practices that deviate grossly from good business conduct, as opposed to good faith behaviour imposed by one trading partner on another. such practices arise where there are imbalances in financial resources and can have a detrimental effect on the union economy as a whole, as they can lead to firms, in particular smes, losing their ability to invest and deciding not to expand their business in the single market. the commission also found that the exporting producer had not provided any evidence that the exporting producer had engaged in dumping during the rip. the commission should be able to take into account the impact of the measures in the member states and the impact of the measures in the union on the level of protection of consumers. i support the motion for a resolution because i believe that the adoption of common standards will allow a labour market in which there are fair and transparent relations between all parties involved in the food supply chain.
written. ‒i voted in favour of this report, but with reservations, because of certain ambiguities in the text relating to the introduction and regulation of new genetic technologies in eu agriculture.
written. ‒ i voted against the european parliament resolution on technical solutions for sustainable agriculture in the eu because, while i support technological progress and a new approach to agriculture, i also believe that we need to be very cautious when it comes to individual agricultural innovations and a progressive approach. in that context, i do not support the current market trend that we all eat the same. the european union cannot be the sole producer of food either, but it is necessary to ensure that each continent and country is able to provide its own diversified food production. i further submit that all necessary precautions should be taken to ensure that health and the environment are not compromised and therefore i cannot support this report.
written. ‒ the world's population is growing and is estimated to reach 9.6 billion by 2050, resulting in a 70% increase in food demand. this report seeks to bring together the possibilities for ensuring an active european agricultural sector, which will develop innovative solutions and technologies in all types of agriculture. the eu should become a world leader in agricultural technology, innovation and sustainability. the eu and member states, including the academic community, breeders, farmers and food producers, need to work together to improve the transition from research to practice. it is also important to establish a regulatory environment that is more conducive to innovation and ensures that eu rules are not an obstacle. with land being reduced, the environment degraded, water scarce, energy demands increasing, and new pests emerging, the natural environment is under pressure, and farmers find it increasingly difficult to produce food sustainably. i supported this report because it did not accept an amendment which sought to allow other land uses, including urbanization, industry, tourism and recreation, which are in competition with agricultural land.

written. ‒ the first information technology trade enhancement agreement (ita) was concluded at the singapore ministerial conference in december 1996 and entered into force in 1997. today, ita has 82 members and covers 97% of the market in the wto sector. the extension of the ita agreement aims at eliminating import duties for 201 it products not covered by the original ita agreement. it is expected to eliminate tariffs on $1.3 trillion in trade, which should boost the world economy by $190 billion. the products covered by the agreement include new generations of semiconductors, gps navigation systems and medical devices. the customs duties on these products will be phased out, with immediate effect for 65% of the products and for all products within seven years. the european commission estimates that the eu will lose approximately eur 1,5 billion in tariffs on it products as a result of the extension of the ita. however, this loss will also be spread over 7 years. i supported this recommendation because i believe that the extension of the ita will result in lower prices for consumers but also for producers and that this will stimulate both job creation and gdp growth.

written. ‒ i give my consent to the conclusion of the agreement in the form of a declaration on the expansion of trade in information technology products. the first information technology agreement (ita) was concluded at the singapore ministerial conference in december 1996 and entered into force in 1997. originally signed by only 29 member countries of the world trade organization, the agreement now has 82 signatories. the agreement on information technology commits each signatory to eliminate customs duties and to impose a zero duty rate on all information technology products covered by that agreement, in accordance with the most-favoured-nation principle. the agreement covers some 200 tariff items, including computers, telephones, but also raw materials, components and machinery for the production of it products. the duty-free regime introduced by the signatories of the itas has played an important role in the rapid development and expansion of trade in the it sector during the almost 20 years of the agreement. trade in that sector has quadrupled. however, with technological advances in that period, the it sector was completely transformed, while the scope of that agreement remained the same. it is for this very reason that i consider it necessary to align the scope of that agreement with technological progress in the information technology sector.

written. ‒ this interim report proposes to find a positive solution in cooperation with the council and the commission, which is in the interest of the union, as it is important to have a harmonised liability regime for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea. the rapporteur considers that it would not be appropriate for parliament to give its consent before the uniformity, integrity and effectiveness of union law and the fundamental principle of eu competence allocation are guaranteed. this interim report is not an obstacle to the establishment of a uniform regime of liability, but represents an effort to ensure it in the most effective and equitable way. maritime transport is a global sector with cross-border impacts, so an international regime is more appropriate than regional solutions to ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for damage caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances by sea across the eu. this will ensure that sufficient funds are available to compensate victims of such accidents. that's why i endorsed this report.
‒ the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, 1996 (hns convention), as amended in 2010, is the last of the international maritime organization (imo) conventions on liability and compensation for damage caused by the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea that has not yet been ratified by all member states and has not entered into force to date. the objective of the proposed council decision is to authorise member states to ratify or accede, on behalf of the union, to the protocol to the 2010 hns convention, which aims to ensure uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation in respect of accidents involving dangerous and noxious substances caused by maritime transport within the territory of the eu and to provide sufficient resources to compensate for losses suffered by natural, legal and public persons and to remedy the damage caused by such accidents. the application of this convention and the protocol is also of importance for croatian citizens in the light of the further strengthening of maritime transport in the adriatic, as it ensures adequate, prompt and effective compensation for all affected stakeholders for loss of or damage to property or the environment resulting from accidents related to the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea.
written. ‒ the objective of the 2010 convention on hazardous and noxious substances is to ensure accountability and adequate, prompt and effective compensation for loss or damage to persons, property or the environment caused by the transport of dangerous and noxious substances by sea, through a specialised international compensation fund. i am in favour of ratifying and acceding to the 2010 protocol to the international convention on hazardous and noxious substances, which provides for the application of the 'polluter pays' principle and the 'precautionary principle' in order to take preventive measures in the event of potential damage to the environment, and therefore falls within the policy area of the union and its fundamental environmental principles. the swift ratification of the protocol is welcome, but it would be even better if the council reconsidered its position and took into account that it is not good for the eu, or its citizens, to create legal uncertainty and differences between the different legal regimes of the member states. i therefore call on the council to adopt a better decision which does not imply differences in the legal regulation of the different member states, especially since the loss or damage to persons, property or the environment caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea often has a cross-border element.
written. ‒ the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, 2010, decides on the strict liability of the owner of a ship carrying harmful substances for any damage caused under these circumstances. the exemption from this liability arises from the obligation of the owner to have insurance to cover the costs. a fund has also been established to compensate for damage caused by the shipowners and insurers. there's no way to pay the victims right now if it goes beyond the owner's liability. the commission has also found that the provisions of the convention on the protection of the rights of the child are not applicable to the protection of children under the age of 18. since the transport of dangerous and harmful substances constitutes a large part of maritime traffic, an international regime would be more appropriate than a regional one to ensure rules on liability and compensation. i supported the report by the freedom mp on the creation of a coherent policy to deal with liability and compensation for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea.

written. ‒ the international convention on hazardous and noxious substances establishes strict liability of the owner of a ship carrying hazardous and noxious substances for any damage caused by an incident related to the maritime transport of hazardous and noxious substances loaded on that ship. the term 'custodian' means any natural or legal person, entity or body that is the ultimate owner of a financial asset or a financial liability of a financial institution, or an entity or body that is the ultimate owner of a financial asset or a financial liability of a financial institution. furthermore, a special compensation fund has been established to pay compensation to all persons who suffer damage related to the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea in the event that those persons have not been able to obtain full and adequate compensation from the shipowner and his insurer. i support this report because i believe that it is necessary to ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation in relation to accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea throughout the eu and that for the maritime sector, as a global sector with cross-border impact, an international regime is more appropriate than a regional one.
‒ the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, 1996 (the 1996 hns convention), as well as the 2010 hns protocol, are the last of a series of conventions of the international maritime organisation relating to liability and compensation for damage caused by the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea that have not yet entered into force. the scope of the 1996 and 2010 hns conventions overlaps with directive 2004/35/ec as regards the liability of economic operators for professional activities, including maritime transport, which do not provide for compensation to victims. the conclusion of the 2010 protocol to the hns convention will ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for damage in relation to accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea throughout the eu. in addition, it will ensure that sufficient funds are available to compensate victims of such accidents. i support this report because i believe that, in order to ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation in relation to accidents caused by ships carrying dangerous and harmful substances at sea throughout the eu, an international regime is more appropriate than regional solutions.

‒ the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, 1996, is the latest in a series of international maritime organisation (imo) conventions relating to liability and compensation for damage caused by the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, which includes both liquefied natural gas (lng) and liquefied petroleum gas (lpg) and has not yet been ratified. the imo has adopted this international agreement to complement the system of maritime liability conventions with a specialised instrument. the 2010 hns convention establishes strict liability of the owner of a ship carrying dangerous and harmful substances for any damage caused by an incident related to the maritime transport of dangerous and harmful substances on board that ship. the hns convention aims to ensure accountability and adequate, prompt and effective compensation for loss. the 1996 hns convention and the 2010 protocol to the hns convention have not entered into force. this report considers that it is in the interest of the union as a whole to have a harmonised liability regime for environmental damage caused by the transport of dangerous and harmful substances by sea, which can only be achieved if the council and the commission give due consideration to parliament's recommendations. i believe that an international regime is more appropriate than regional solutions to solve this problem. that's why i endorsed this report.
‒ the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea (hns convention) of 1996, as amended in 2010, is the latest in a series of international maritime organization (imo) conventions relating to liability and compensation for damage caused by the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea. liability and compensation for damage arising from shipping activities are regulated at international level by a series of imo conventions which rely on strict liability of the shipowner, compulsory insurance to cover damage caused to third parties, the right of injured persons to seek compensation directly from the insurer, limitation of liability and, in the case of oil and dangerous and noxious substances, the use of a special compensation fund from which to pay damages if such damages exceed the limits of the shipowner's liability. the objective of the proposed council decision is linked to the danish exemption from the application of the aspects relating to judicial cooperation in civil matters contained in the proposal for a protocol. for the above reasons, i have supported this decision.

president-in-office of the council. – mr president, i would like to thank mr la via for this important question. the european union and its member states are strongly committed to the protection of whales. and in a broader sense i think you mention exactly why this is so important: the protection of biodiversity and marine ecosystems. let me also be very clear about the position of the council. we do not approve of the current whaling activities of japan. up to this day, japan has failed to present sufficient evidence to justify its whaling activities with regard to its new research programme and a justification of lethal sampling, in particular, is far below standard. we have conveyed our serious concerns in view of the expert panel findings and the conclusions of the scientific committee, and our position has not changed since june 2015. these serious concerns will be expressed again in a meeting in october and we acknowledge that an effective conservation and management regime can only be established through joint efforts and by initiatives that promote mutual trust and cooperation between all the members of the international whaling commission. as already said, and i think you mentioned this very important point, at the international whaling commission meeting in september 2014, we regard the judgment delivered by the international court of justice in march 2014 concerning whaling in the antarctic as a definitive interpretation of the convention, and we believe that the principles of the icj judgment should be fully incorporated into the working practices, including by a revision of the current review system, annex b. in our view the judgment clarifies the legal framework for scientific whaling, particularly when it comes to assessing the necessity of having recourse to lethal methods of sampling where non-lethal alternatives exist. the judgment can also help to ensure an effective regulatory framework for international conservation and management. this brings all whaling operations under iwc control. the european union and its member states stand by iwc resolution 2014-5 adopted in 2014, according to which no further whaling permit should be granted without prior international review, including by the iwc scientific committee. we regret that japan had not consulted with its partners before engaging in such activities, which are not in line with the icj ruling. the presidency will ensure that the european union and its member states are well prepared for the upcoming meeting in october. it is also against this background that the european union and its member states joined the démarche led by new zealand to japan in december 2015 following the resumption of japan's whaling activities in the southern ocean.
vice-president of the commission. – mr president, the eu is fully committed to the conservation of all cetaceans and is equipped with environmental legislation to pursue this objective. commercial whaling is not allowed in member states’ waters or by ships under the jurisdiction of a member state. all whale species are protected from deliberate disturbance, capture or killing under the habitats directive. in addition, the introduction of cetaceans into, and export from, the eu for primarily commercial purposes is banned under our wildlife regulations. the eu has also clearly positioned itself against commercial whaling at the international whaling commission and strongly supports the moratorium on commercial whaling as an essential measure to protect whale stocks that have been decimated by decades and decades of unsustainable hunts. for many decades now japan has been conducting so-called scientific whaling under the special permit provided under the international convention on the regulation of whaling. the eu welcomed the 2014 landmark judgment delivered by the international court of justice ordering the interruption of the japanese research programme in the arctic, in the light of its scale, methods and limited scientific output. in december 2015, the eu and its member states joined new zealand, australia, the usa, mexico and south africa in a diplomatic démarche towards the japanese authorities against the decision to issue special permits under its new scientific whale research programme in the antarctic ocean for the hunting season 2015-2016. the eu and its member states do not believe that lethal sampling is required to satisfy the needs of a modern scientific research programme. in addition, we are deeply concerned by the fact that the new japanese programme has been launched without due recourse to the concerns expressed by the iwc scientific committee in line with the clear criteria identified by the icj defining whaling for the purpose of scientific research. regrettably our diplomatic initiative did not result in reconsideration of the decision by the government of japan. the issue of scientific whaling will be again on the agenda of the iwc at its next meeting, which will take place in slovenia in october. the eu will continue to take a strong position on this subject and to work with our international partners to press for decisions within the iwc that lead to better conservation of whales worldwide. the commission is not considering legal action against japan at this stage. we should try to resolve the issue through political dialogue as well as further discussions in the competent international forum, the iwc. the overall objective of the eu is to ensure an effective international regulatory framework for conservation and management, that currently is a significant improvement in the conservation status of whales in the long term and that brings all whaling operations under iwc control.

member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is a pleasure to be here today, once again, to take part in this debate on two of the most important pillars of the energy union: energy efficiency and renewable energy. moreover, addressing them at the same time reflects the important role they both play in meeting the ambitious climate commitments reached at the last paris summit. and the debate is coming at a very appropriate time, as we are finalising the review of energy efficiency and renewable energy legislation, which will be published in the second half of the year. let me begin by thanking the two rapporteurs for their excellent work on these important own-initiative reports. i shall start with mr pieper's report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive. as you know, we are preparing the revisions of the energy efficiency and energy efficiency in buildings directives. the purpose is to set energy efficiency targets for 2030 and to ensure that we have the right framework and measures in place to achieve them and, by focusing on buildings in particular, we are giving priority to sectors with the greatest potential for energy savings. the report draws a number of conclusions which we will take into account in preparing the reviews i have just mentioned. i fully agree with the conclusion of the pieper report on the need to systematically include the principle of energy efficiency first in our energy and climate policies. let me also say that europe needs an explicit target for 2030 that is embedded in legislation. it will be important in sending a positive signal to investors and policymakers and in boosting the long-term investments we need to meet our objectives. but the revision of our energy legislation needs to go far beyond a final objective. we need to take compliance and enforcement seriously. in this connection, let me stress the fact that the review of the energy efficiency directive will address article 7, energy saving obligations. the recent evaluation showed that member states have taken this policy seriously, have taken the necessary measures and have put in place control and verification systems to achieve the necessary savings by 2020. it is expected that by 2020 this article could contribute to about half of the savings of the energy efficiency directive. it has been an effective instrument, but we now need to align it with the overall 2030 framework so that it can contribute to the ambitious emission reduction targets set at the european council in october 2014. it will also be important to encourage private investment in our buildings, a sector with enormous savings potential, a sector key not only to achieving our energy efficiency targets, but also to tackling energy poverty, reducing high energy bills and reducing health risks. the review of the energy efficiency in buildings directive will pay particular attention to these objectives. i would like to thank the rapporteur once again for including these important matters in his report, and we have to work closely on these legislative proposals. of course, this also applies to the revision of the renewable energy directive. this is a directive that has worked well. with a share of renewables of 16% of final energy consumption in 2014, the european union and a majority of member states are making good progress towards the 2020 targets. all but one country is ahead of its indicative trajectory and nine have already reached their 2020 targets. this has allowed us to cut our fossil fuel imports, reduce emissions and develop a competitive renewable energy industry. however, some member states need to step up their efforts to keep up with the intense trajectory we need to maintain in the coming years. that is why we are fully focused on the implementation of the renewable energy directive and i know that this is fundamental for the european parliament. but as the report rightly points out, we also need to look beyond 2020. the review of the renewable energy directive will be the central pillar of these efforts and will be reinforced by the redesign of the electricity market and the energy union governance initiative. as many of you have asked, we want to put on the table a robust legal framework that gives stability to investors and helps us achieve our objectives efficiently. our ambition is that the revision of the renewables directive, the redesign of the electricity market and the reinforced emissions trading system will be key drivers for new investments in renewables that will help europe become number one in this sector. in the review of the renewable energy directive we intend to address many of the concerns reflected in its amendments. for example, how to better harness the potential of renewable energy in the heating and cooling sector and how to incentivise the role of the consumer. we are also working to remove the administrative and institutional barriers which hold back investment in europe. let me give you an idea of the elements we're considering. first, on targets we need to build on the progress made by 2020. so we're exploring setting the 2020 national targets as a starting point. secondly, the directive will concentrate on three sectors which will help us to achieve our objectives: electricity, heating and cooling, and transport. in particular, we share your concern about the slow progress in the transport sector. thirdly, another key point will be the role of support schemes for renewables. in our proposal we will consolidate the shift towards a market-based system for support mechanisms for renewables and towards convergence of national support schemes. as i have already mentioned, we plan to move towards better market design, which, together with a strengthened emissions trading system, will make it easier for renewable energy generators to get the maximum benefit from the market. finally, we have seen in this report that the question of the sustainability criteria for bioenergy is of considerable interest. the commission is working on an enhanced sustainability policy for biofuels and biomass. biomass is the main source of renewable energy in the european union and we are looking for a pragmatic approach that ensures considerable emission savings, avoids risks of significant environmental impacts and avoids unnecessary administrative burdens, especially for small power plants and small forest owners. ladies and gentlemen, let me conclude by stressing the importance i attach to this debate and to the contribution of the european parliament to the preparation of future legislative proposals. i would like to mention one last aspect which i believe is of great importance in order to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves. i am referring to the need to mobilise investment in these sectors. the european fund for strategic investments has opened the door to new possibilities which we must exploit wisely, and i would like to call on local, regional and national authorities to make greater use of this instrument. i would like to conclude by saying that the commission is very grateful for these two reports. i assure you that in the coming legislative proposals we will be ambitious and ensure that energy efficiency and renewable energy are the key drivers of our paris commitments and our transition towards the decarbonisation of our energy system, and i look forward to working closely with the european parliament to make this noble cause possible.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco concerning measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec (com (((2016) 0201 c8-0157/2016 2016/0109 ((nle))), as that agreement is an important step in the current efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and constitutes an upgrade of the previous agreement of 2004. the eu member states and monaco shall exchange information on the financial accounts held by nationals of the other party automatically, as from 2018, for information collected since 1 january 2017.
written. ‒ the importance of automatic exchange of information on financial accounts as a means of combating cross-border tax fraud and cross-border tax evasion at international level is high. that is why a single global standard for the automatic exchange of information was developed and published in july 2014. i consider that the expansion of mandatory automatic exchange of information between competent tax administrations in the union, and in line with the global standard, is necessary and desirable. given that the taxation of savings directive has been repealed and that directive 2014/107/eu amending directive 2011/16/eu with regard to the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation applies, it is necessary to amend the existing taxation of savings agreements with switzerland, andorra, liechtenstein, monaco and san marino. in this context, i have supported this report and the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the amending protocol to the agreement between the european community and the principality of monaco. the amendment protocol will implement a global standard between the member states and monaco, which will certainly contribute to the transparency of the tax and financial system of the union.
‒ the eu and monaco have reached an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, which aims to improve tax cooperation and enforcement at international level. the agreement is an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and is an upgrade of the 2004 agreement, which guarantees that monaco applies measures equivalent to those in the eu directive on taxation of savings income on interest. the agreement provides for the automatic exchange of information on the financial accounts held by nationals of the other party in the territory of the european union and monaco, as from 2018, for information collected since 1 january 2017. the aim is to tackle situations where taxpayers want to conceal capital representing income or assets that have not been taxed. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the financial instruments are used for the purpose of the provision of financial services. i fully welcome and support the agreement.
‒ the european union and monaco have negotiated an agreement providing for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, with a view to improving international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement is an important step in the fight against tax evasion and tax fraud and builds on the 2004 agreement by which monaco started applying measures equivalent to those required by the eu savings tax directive. the new agreement will provide for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts between the member states and monaco, with the main objective of responding adequately to situations in which taxpayers attempt to avoid paying taxes. i support this report because i believe that monaco should apply measures equivalent to the legislative framework of the european union, which are in line with the procedures for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts.
‒ the european union and monaco have agreed on an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts with a view to improving international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement represents an important step in the process of combating tax fraud and tax evasion. the agreement provides for the automatic exchange of information between the member states of the union and monaco on financial accounts in their territories as from 2018 for information collected as from 1 january 2017. the agreement will also provide for the exchange of information on the tax treatment of individuals and businesses in monaco, including on the tax treatment of individuals and businesses in monaco. i support the adoption of this agreement because i believe that it will address situations where a taxpayer seeks to conceal capital representing income or assets for which he has not paid tax.
written. ‒ i supported the agreement between the european union and the principality of monaco providing for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. the automatic exchange of information is of great importance as a means of combating cross-border tax fraud and cross-border tax evasion by ensuring full tax transparency and systematic cooperation between tax administrations worldwide. the g20 entrusted the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) with the task of developing a single global standard for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, and the oecd council published that global standard in july 2014. the parties shall cooperate to ensure that the information is provided in a manner that is consistent with the principles of confidentiality and integrity of the information.

written. ‒ in view of the reduction in production in one entire manufacturing sector in belgium, the production of machinery and equipment, which resulted in the dismissal of as many as 488 workers in the hainaut region who were declared surplus, and given that the eu has the instruments but also the obligation to help workers affected by major structural changes, i supported the decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund on the basis of a request submitted by belgium. i am pleased that, in addition to the workers made redundant, the financial assistance received from the fund will also be used to create new opportunities and jobs for the unemployed young people, who are very numerous in the region. the belgian region of hainaut is facing a difficult labour market situation, with an employment rate of 52,7%. the commission notes that the walloon region has not provided any evidence that the aid granted to the walloon region was compatible with the internal market. on the other hand, the labour market in hainaut is characterised by a high proportion of under-qualified workers (just over half of jobseekers have not completed secondary education), so it is important to invest in orientation and training measures and in the development of skills adapted to the needs.

‒ caterpillar belgium sa has made 1399 redundancies in the hainaut region, where the current unemployment rate is high at 14,5% (5,9% above the national average), due to the significant rise in steel prices in europe. the report notes that the fund will finance integrated training of workers, start-up aid and joint projects, as well as the costs of job search and training allowances. given that the union is committed to providing financial assistance to workers declared redundant as a result of the economic crisis as soon as possible, it is essential that this proposal be adopted as soon as possible. i support the report of the committee on budgets, since the launch of the fund for adaptation to globalisation in hainaut (be32) will enable it to provide additional support to workers and unemployed young people who are affected by the decline in the competitiveness of european producers.

written. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund provides support to people who have lost their jobs as a result of significant structural changes in world trade flows due to globalisation, the closure of large companies or the relocation of production outside the european union, or as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. belgium has submitted an application under this programme egf/2015/012 be/hainaut machinery for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund, following redundancies in the economic sector. as a member of the european parliament, i support all measures to create jobs and growth, but i do not consider the european globalisation adjustment fund to be an effective tool for reintegrating surplus workers and i do not support its work in principle and i voted against this report.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009 (com (2015) 0180c8-0118/2015 2015/0096 ((cod)) as this regulation seeks to ensure the uniform and effective application in the european union of all measures under the recovery plan adopted between 2012 and 2014, which, together with the previous measures since 2008, has contributed to exceptional results in terms of the conservation of bluefin tuna and allows for a gradual increase in the total catches without compromising the results achieved. the commission has also proposed to amend the catch reporting system in order to ensure that the catch reporting system is more transparent and that the catch reporting system is more transparent.
‒ the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas has adopted measures for a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan (bft) in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean sea, which will apply from 2007 to 2022. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the establishment of a european union reference laboratory for the assessment of the effects of the use of the biocidal products referred to in paragraph 1 of this article. such common fisheries policies are necessary to preserve the good state of the fisheries and to ensure the most efficient exploitation of marine resources. i particularly welcome two sections of this report. first, advocating the role of traditional tools and techniques in the conservation of fish stocks, because i believe that in implementing the eu bluefin tuna recovery plan, these tools and techniques should be given special consideration because of their selectivity. secondly, i welcome the inclusion in this plan of catching vessels flying the flag of the republic of croatia, which extends the existing number established in 2008 and takes into account the accession of the republic of croatia to the eu and its efforts to conserve bluefin tuna.
written. ‒ each member state shall take the necessary measures to ensure that the fishing effort of its catching vessels and tuna trap operators is commensurate with the fishing opportunities for bluefin tuna available to that member state in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean. the maximum number and the corresponding gross tonnage of fishing vessels flying the flag of a member state fishing for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean shall not exceed the number and the total corresponding gross tonnage of fishing vessels flying the flag of that member state which have caught, retained on board, transhipped, transported or landed bluefin tuna during the period from 1 january 2007 to 1 july 2008. the fishing opportunities set out in this regulation shall be managed in accordance with the management plan established by the union. the flag member state shall withdraw the authorisation to fish bluefin tuna and may require the vessel to proceed immediately to a port designated by it if it considers that the vessel has exhausted its quota. i consider that, with the amendments annexed, a proposal for a council and european parliament regulation on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009 is essential if we are to see progress on the recovery of bluefin tuna in those areas.
