written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean and repealing regulation (ec) no 302/2009. the objective of this proposal is to transpose into union law the measures of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean sea adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas at its annual meetings from 2012 to 2014. this regulation lays down the general rules of the tuna recovery plan, while taking into account the specificities of the different gears, with particular attention to traditional and sustainable gears and gears used in small-scale coastal fishing, such as tuna traps. this legislative initiative will address the issues of ensuring the uniform and effective application of the latest measures of the iccat multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan throughout the european union.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, amending council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007 (com (2014) 0614 c8 0174/2014 2014/0285 (cod)) as it is a multiannual management plan that takes into account several species that are interlinked and interact. it is also important because these three species - cod, herring and sprat - in the baltic sea account for over 94% of catches in recent years and there are risks of overfishing and the consequences for the ecosystem of the closure of the baltic. such a plan can serve to develop other management and exploitation plans for fish stocks in other seas, for fish that interact with each other. the management approach of the union should be based on the principle of sustainable exploitation of the stocks, and should be based on the principle of sustainable exploitation of the resources of the union.
written. ‒ the current regulations for managing the baltic sea stocks have covered only cod, and this stock has also been assessed as being disproportionate to the current situation of cod stocks and the fisheries that depend on it, which may undermine the stability of the baltic sea ecosystem. since herring and mackerel are also present in the baltic sea and are in constant interaction with cod and are therefore an integral part of the baltic sea ecosystem, i consider it important to adopt a regulation recognising the mutual influence of these species and regulating the management of their stocks accordingly and for this reason i voted in favour of adopting a multiannual plan for cod, herring and mackerel stocks in the baltic sea. the need to maintain ecosystem balance requires proper care and i consider it a good move to include all stocks of the relevant fish species in a single management plan that can ensure a more efficient and balanced exploitation of those stocks and the stability of traditional fisheries, given that the current exploitation rates of cod, herring and sprat stocks are not consistent with achieving the maximum sustainable yield. the model of this multiannual plan could lead to similar plans for fisheries in other geographical areas, with constant reference to the latest scientific research.
the united nations convention of 10 december 1982 on the law of the sea, to which the union is a party, provides for conservation obligations, including the maintenance or restoration of populations of harvested species at levels capable of producing the highest sustainable yield, as determined by appropriate environmental and economic factors. the management plan for a large number of species established by this regulation requires that greater account be taken of the different ecological roles and functions of the species covered by the plan; as the various species are highly interacting, catches cannot be maximally sustainable for all species at the same time and decisions need to be taken on which species to give priority. the exploitation of cod and pelagic stocks shall not jeopardise the sustainability of the stocks taken as by-catch in that fishery, i.e. the stocks of plaice, mackerel, herring and plaice in the baltic. the plan should therefore also aim at ensuring the conservation of those demersal stocks above biomass levels that correspond to the precautionary and ecosystem-based approaches to fisheries management that can produce the highest sustainable yield.
written. ‒ since 2008, a provision on the control of cod catches in the baltic sea has been in force, but the fisheries committee considers that the existing provision does not take into account the current fishing situation in the baltic sea and that it needs to be amended. the existing provisions also do not cover the state of the baltic sea herring and puffins. the committee considers that, in view of the fisheries and the continuing ecological changes in the fisheries habitat, a comprehensive management plan for baltic cod, herring and papalina is needed. it is proposed that management be carried out using the most up-to-date scientific methods, taking into account the consequences for other fish species and the ecology of the baltic sea subsea. the committee recommends that the commission should also monitor the plan if management or fishing has a significant impact on the so-called 'flat fish'. the first review of the plan should take place three years after its entry into force and, if the plan produces positive effects, a second review would follow five years after its establishment. given that the current provisions cover only one species of baltic fish, that the baltic sea is a sensitive habitat and of great economic importance to the member states, and that it covers the possibility of extension to other fish species, i support this report.
written. ‒ the european commission published a multiannual plan for the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea and for the fisheries and exploitation of these stocks in october 2014. the project aims to establish a framework for the management of cod, herring and mackerel stocks in the baltic sea, where fishing is primarily concentrated on these three species. the baltic sea management plan has been in place since 2008, but is not considered to be commensurate with the current cod stock situation. the stocks of herring and of papalina are not yet covered by the management plan. cod, herring and parrotfish are important components of the baltic ecosystem. it is estimated that cod, herring and sprat have accounted for more than 94% of the baltic catches in recent years. it is important to bear in mind that the plan is only an introductory proposal in the very fragile ecosystem of the baltic sea. the first review of the plan should take place three years after its entry into force and, if it has positive effects, it will be revised again after 5 years. this will also provide the much needed flexibility of the plan. i support the position of parliament in adopting the report because i believe that parliament is competent enough to assess whether a report is sufficiently clear and well-formed.
written. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, amending council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007. the objective of this regulation of the european parliament is to establish a fisheries plan for a large number of species taking into account the dynamics between the stocks of cod, herring and sprat and the by-catch of species in the fisheries for those stocks, i.e. goldenseal, sprat, herring and plaice in the baltic. although the baltic cod stock management plan has been in force since 2008, it is considered to be out of proportion to the current cod stock situation and the cod and herring are not covered by the plan. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 21 to amend the list of stocks subject to the landing obligation set out in annex i to regulation (eu) no 1380/2013.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction and the applicable law, and on the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes, because i consider that this proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regimes is clearly in the interest of the union and its international couples. it will remove a number of legal doubts and uncertainties.
written. ‒ while the council regulation on jurisdiction and the applicable law and on the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes would greatly facilitate legal proceedings by international spouses in a situation of divorce or death of one of the spouses, i did not support the proposal for a regulation because the regulation is not sufficiently precisely defined in law and the legal ambiguity and vacuum leads to unintended consequences of granting equal rights to married and other partnerships and puts undue pressure on the family law of the member states. if a single european legislative act is to be adopted, it must first of all clearly define what constitutes marriage, namely that marriage is the union of one man and one woman, which is not specified in the regulation. since nine member states of the european union equate same-sex unions with marriage, the adoption of this regulation would equate marriage and other unions in a totally inappropriate way at eu level. this would also jeopardise the national family policy of member states which have a well-defined institution of marriage and clearly distinguish, or do not regulate, other unions. each member state must retain the freedom to provide legal protection for the institution of marriage, and the distinction between matrimonial and other civil partnerships must be very clearly defined.
written. ‒ this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regime is the second in the series on this subject. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the regulation will be a very useful instrument for international couples within the european union. in the area of matrimonial property regime, it covers jurisdiction and the law applicable as well as the recognition and enforcement of decisions. however, it excludes, in particular, questions of the capacity of spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of marriage, maintenance obligations and succession of the deceased spouse. the autonomy of the member states in family law matters is therefore preserved. the regulation also does not affect the substantive law of the member states on matrimonial property regimes. in other words, parliament's demands were met. in conclusion, i agree with the rapporteur, mr jean-marie cavad, that this proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regimes is clearly in the interest of the union and its international couples. it will remove a number of legal doubts and uncertainties.
written. ‒ the recommendation of the committee on legal affairs simplifies the previously unclear and undefined jurisdiction of the courts on matrimonial property for married couples coming from different member states. the legal entity is entitled to choose the country of which it is a national or the country of which its spouse is a national and to settle matters of succession under the laws of the country of its choice. the recommendation states that any court decisions relating to the bankruptcy are binding, except in 'very specific circumstances'. the recommendation calls for the establishment of an effective means of communicating these rights to all married couples who are not nationals of the same country.
written. ‒ this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes is the second on this subject. the 2016 proposal for a regulation differs from the commission's initial 2011 proposal. on the contrary, it contains many of the amendments proposed by parliament in 2013. the regulation does not cover issues such as the legal capacity of spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of marriage, maintenance obligations. the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law is thus preserved. i support the proposal for this regulation because i believe that it will be a very useful instrument for the rights of international couples in the union. the regulation will put an end to the many cases of legal uncertainty in this area.
written. ‒ the increasing mobility of persons within the area without internal borders has led to a significant increase in the number of couples who are nationals of different member states living in a member state other than their own or acquiring property in more than one member state. the number of international couples within the union is large and the practical and legal difficulties they face in the day-to-day management of their property and in the division of property following the divorce of the couple or the death of one of the members of the couple have been identified, and this proposal seeks to establish a clear legal framework of the european union for determining the jurisdiction and the law applicable to matrimonial property regimes and to facilitate the circulation of decisions and documents between member states. since i consider that this area should remain the responsibility of the member states and that the entry into force of this regulation would lead to a breach of the principle of subsidiarity, i abstained.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships, as this proposal will contribute to the removal of a number of doubts in this area, which is certainly in the interest of the european union and of the international couples living in it.
written. ‒ since this proposal on jurisdiction and the law applicable in matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships was accompanied by a similar proposal on matrimonial property regimes, which has been almost completely adopted, such an attempt to equalise marriage and other civil unions is problematic. the question is inevitable whether some future act will similarly attempt to equalise marriage and other unions in matters of parental care, adoption, and the like. the commission should also be able to assess the compatibility of the proposed amendments with the requirements of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, in particular with the requirements of article 4 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and with the requirements of article 4 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. thus, the impression is given that the registered partnership is imposed on all countries. i did not support the proposal on jurisdiction and applicable law in matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships because i consider that not all the legal elements are sufficiently clearly and precisely defined and that this proposal opens the door to the almost forced harmonisation of other contentious issues related to registered partnerships.
written. ‒ this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction and the applicable law, and on the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships is the second in a series on this subject. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the regulation will be a very useful instrument for international couples within the european union. in the field of property consequences of registered partnerships, it covers jurisdiction and the law applicable as well as the recognition and enforcement of decisions. however, in particular, questions of the legal capacity of the partners, the existence, validity or recognition of the partnership, the maintenance obligation and the succession of the deceased partner are excluded from its scope. the autonomy of the member states in family law matters is therefore preserved. the regulation also does not affect the substantive law of the member states on registered partnerships or their property consequences. the parliament's requests are therefore granted. in conclusion, i agree with the rapporteur, mr jean-marie cavad, that this proposal for a regulation on the property consequences of registered partnerships is clearly in the interest of the union and its international couples. it will remove a number of legal doubts and uncertainties.

written. ‒ the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction and the applicable law, and on the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships is the second in a series on this subject and aims to establish a comprehensive set of rules of private international law applicable to the property consequences of registered partnerships. as in the case of matrimonial property regimes, the property relations between registered partners and between the partners and third parties arise from the prior existence of a registered partnership. the property consequences of registered partnerships arise with the registration of the partnership, just as the matrimonial property regime arises with marriage, and cease with the dissolution of the partnership. the partnership is registered with a public body and establishes a stable and legally recognised relationship. however, i did not support this report because the establishment of a comprehensive set of european union rules on this issue would lead to a breach of the principle of subsidiarity.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver, as this deepens the relations between the two countries. the visa-free stay in the territory of the other contracting party will allow for the strengthening of economic and cultural relations, tourism, and trade and investment. the union is the largest investor in peru and the conclusion of this agreement is of paramount importance in order to strengthen regional coherence, cooperation in the area of illegal migration and dialogue on fundamental freedoms and human rights. therefore, i support this recommendation.
written. ‒ the eu is peru's third trading partner in terms of imports (mainly machinery and transport equipment) and its main export partner (agricultural and food products and ores). in addition, the eu remains the largest investor in peru and is responsible for more than 50% of total foreign direct investment in sectors such as banking and finance. the republic of peru has a relatively stable democracy and in this respect is an important partner of the union in latin america. the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver will deepen relations between the eu and the republic of peru and further strengthen economic and cultural relations and political dialogue on human rights and fundamental freedoms. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the visa waiver and the visa-free regime in the member states. the agreement also contains a joint declaration on cooperation in the area of illegal migration, thus enabling peru to become a key partner in the fight against organised crime, in particular drug and human trafficking. i consider that the abolition of short-stay visas is a necessary element in the process of rapprochement between the eu and peru, and i therefore supported this recommendation.

‒ regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council replaced regulation (ec) no 539/2001 and moved the republic of peru to annex ii, which contains the list of countries whose nationals may cross the external borders of the member states without being required to be in possession of a visa. the amended regulation applies in all member states of the european union except ireland and the united kingdom. the situation in the republic of peru has been examined in detail and all possibilities that may arise from the visa liberalisation have been assessed. on 19 may 2015, the council adopted a decision authorising the commission to conclude the bilateral agreement as it had received a positive assessment following a further evaluation of the situation in peru. the agreement was signed on 14 march 2016 in brussels. the agreement guarantees visa-free travel for the citizens of the european union and peru for a maximum period of 90 days in the territory of the other party. i support this recommendation for a draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver, as i consider that peru has fulfilled all the conditions for visa liberalisation and as i consider that this agreement benefits the free and unhindered movement of people between the two parties to the agreement.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on combating trafficking in human beings in the eu's external relations (2015/2340 ((ini)) as i support the efforts of the eu, the member states and partner countries to tackle this widespread and unfortunately lucrative criminal activity. the consequences of human trafficking are frightening. these include modern slavery, child exploitation, prostitution, begging, potential security risks, violations of basic human rights, one of the worst forms of denial of human dignity, murder, organ trafficking, and the growing strength of criminal organizations. it is not enough to deal with this problem only in the internal territory of the eu countries. the eu needs to develop its own policy, adopt a strategy and implement actions and strengthen cooperation with third countries where the source of the problem is located. the eu should support the development of a functioning state, legal, legislative and security system in the most vulnerable countries, particularly those in the neighbourhood, to be able to deal with criminal groups involved in trafficking in human beings. the fight against criminal networks involved in trafficking in human beings requires an international response where the eu needs to take a leading role, in particular in cooperation with countries in the immediate vicinity.
written. ‒ human trafficking, alongside illegal drugs and arms trafficking, is one of the most lucrative activities of organised crime in the world. according to the latest world slavery index, 35.8 million people worldwide are victims of modern-day slavery. some 14.2 million are forced to live in conditions of forced labor, 4.5 million suffer forced sexual exploitation, and 2.2 million are in a state-imposed position of forced labor. the report condemns the practice of trafficking in human beings and regrets that in many countries of the world, adequate legislation to effectively combat trafficking in human beings has not yet been enacted. trafficking in human beings is different from the smuggling of migrants and therefore a different legal and practical framework needs to be applied. it is important that strategies to prevent trafficking in human beings also take into account the factors that facilitate trafficking. the eu must develop a new strategy to combat trafficking in human beings with a stronger and more prominent external dimension for the period after 2016. in this context, recognition of victims of trafficking in human beings is important to enable them to exercise their rights, including access to justice, legal recognition of identity and citizenship, restitution of property, adequate compensation, and medical and psychological care and long-term integration assistance. i agree with the points made and therefore supported this report.

written. ‒ the objective of the proposed code is to ensure a high common level of network and information security (nis). this means improving the security of the internet, the private networks and information systems that support the functioning of our society and economy. the proposal requires all member states to ensure a minimum level of national capacity by setting up competent authorities for network and information security (nis), establishing computer security incident response teams (csirts), adopting national strategies and national cooperation plans for nis, and obliging operators in certain sectors, including internet service providers, energy, transport, financial markets, health, as well as public administration administrators, to share nis incident reporting and adopt appropriate measures to secure nis. the proposal introduces a network and information security (nis) obligation to create a level playing field and close existing loopholes, which is why i supported this proposal.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on japan's decision to continue whaling in the 2015/16 season because i believe that the international community needs to do more to preserve biodiversity and marine ecosystems, especially when it comes to conserving endangered species. in this context, the number of whales being killed using special permits for purported scientific research has increased, directly threatening the whale population as a whole. japan is a strategic partner of the eu and bilateral cooperation is based on the rules of the international order. therefore, i support the call to japan to stop whaling and to maintain a global moratorium on commercial whaling, and i continue to support this joint motion for a resolution.
the international whaling commission adopted a moratorium on all forms of commercial whaling in 1982 to protect stocks from extinction and allow them to recover. this moratorium, which is still in force, allows for exemptions for whaling of only a limited number of animals for scientific purposes only, so-called 'special permit whaling'. despite a moratorium on commercial whaling, the practice continues in some countries, and the number of whales killed under special permits for purported scientific research is on the rise. japan has been practicing this form of whaling for decades. in a judgment of 31 march 2014, the international tribunal ordered the suspension of the annual whaling in japan, based on its jarpa ii programme, due to the lack of scientific value and the fact that the issued permits were not used for scientific research. the commission has also received information from the japanese authorities, which has provided it with a copy of the notification. the commission has also provided information on the number of vessels that have been involved in the illegal whaling operation in the baltic sea. i supported this resolution as the primary objectives must be the protection of biodiversity, including the conservation of species, while respecting the eu habitats directive, which does not allow commercial whaling.
written. ‒ i supported the resolution on japan's decision to resume whaling in the 2015/16 season. whether we consider the ban on whales to be appropriate and justified or not, it is based on an international agreement that dates back to 1931 and to 1946, when the dangers of overfishing were first recognized. that cooperation resulted in a moratorium some 30 years ago. this step was based on scientific research that speaks to the need to conserve and recover populations that have been decimated by previous unsustainable whaling practices. in those years, 50,000 whales were caught a year. it is unfortunate that the 1982 whaling moratorium is not enforced, and in the last 30 years, despite the ban, japan has hunted 20,000 whales under the guise of scientific research. it is the disregard for international law and the judgment of the international court of justice that is particularly worrying. this disrespect is evident in the decision to continue whaling and the planned capture of another 4,000 whales over the next 12 years. i wonder what would happen if other countries were to disregard international agreements to the same degree. let us not forget that the whaling fleets of canada, the faroe islands, greenland, iceland, indonesia, norway, the philippines, russia, st. vincent and the grenadines, south korea, and the united states are also entitled to whaling.
written. ‒ in 1982, the international whaling commission, in an effort to protect the stocks from extinction and enable them to recover, imposed a moratorium on all forms of commercial whaling, which is still in effect. the international whaling convention contains specific provisions allowing the whaling of a limited number of animals for scientific purposes only, known as 'special permit whaling'. despite this international ban, which came into force in 1986, japan continued to hunt whales and by 2014 had killed more than 20,000 whales. in october 2015, japan submitted a declaration to the un accepting the icj's ruling with the exception of any dispute arising out of, relating to or related to the exploration, conservation, management or exploitation of marine biological resources, effectively excluding any future objections to the icj regarding their specific whaling licence programmes. for all of the above, i call on japan to suspend whaling and to respect the findings of the international whaling commission. i also strongly support maintaining a worldwide moratorium on commercial whaling and banning international trade in whale products. i call for an end to unwarranted 'whaling for scientific purposes' and support the designation of large ocean and marine areas as sanctuaries where all forms of whaling are banned indefinitely.

written. ‒ the key to greater participation of women in the labour market is quality institutions that would make it easier for them to reconcile private and professional obligations. i am thinking primarily of quality care for children in kindergartens and nurseries. also, a better network of care facilities needs to be developed, since women often bear the burden of caring for older family members. the second element that is important is the professional empowerment of women, through the fight against gendered occupational determination and the 'breaking of the glass ceiling'.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on creating favourable conditions in the labour market for achieving a balance between private and professional life, as i support the idea of european legislation being actively introduced on this issue as well. social and working conditions are changing rapidly, with consequences for lifestyles and quality of life. the reconciliation of private and professional life is an issue we encounter every day and affects family status, birth rate, quality of work and competitiveness of companies, general satisfaction, upbringing and conditions of education, social and economic status and numerous other facts that define the business and private environment and affect the quality of life now and in the near future. i agree with the fact that the reconciliation of work, private and family life should be guaranteed as a fundamental right for all people. it is necessary to introduce a framework to ensure that right within the social systems of the eu and the member states. models that achieve a work-life balance need to be promoted and all eu activities that have an impact on this issue should be included.
written. ‒ parents today face many problems in balancing family and work life, and women are exposed to various forms of discrimination at work from the very access to employment for planned future pregnancy, through the denial or reduction of their labour rights or maternity benefits, even to dismissal. the problem of working long hours and working without days off, weekends, holidays and public holidays is becoming more common, and it particularly affects shop workers. a non-working week in all eu member states would allow families to spend quality time together that is not guaranteed during the working week, especially in families where both spouses work or where the working parent is the sole provider of their children. the family and children must be at the heart of all work-life balance policies and it is unacceptable that these policies, under the guise of protecting workers' and women's rights, attempt to redefine the family as the fundamental unit of society. i could not therefore support this resolution because i believe that it does not deal with real problems but instead of proposing concrete solutions to create a balance between family and professional life, it tries to impose ideological issues and redefine the family based on marriage between a man and a woman.
‒ in 2015, in the 28 eu member states, the employment rate for men was 75,9% compared to the employment rate for women, which was 64,3%, despite the fact that women were more educated; whereas the number of women in the labour force is even lower when taking into account the full-time employment rate, given that the share of part-time employment among women is very high in some member states; whereas in 2013, men were paid for 47 hours of work per week and women for 34 hours; whereas, when hours of paid and unpaid work at home are added together, young women worked an average of 64 hours and young men 53. the losses of gdp per capita attributable to gender differences in the labour market are estimated to be up to 10% in europe. i consider this unacceptable and i agree with the calls that we must do everything in our power to reduce the gap as soon as possible and to eliminate it completely. in view of the above, i support the adoption of the report.

written. ‒ i abstained on the report on creating favourable conditions in the labour market for achieving a balance between private and professional life. although i understand the importance of work-life balance, i could not support this report for several reasons. one of the main reasons is that it repeatedly violates the principle of subsidiarity, i.e. the report ignores the competence of the member states over certain areas. in addition, i am firmly of the view that families, i.e. workers, must be able to determine for themselves how they will reconcile private time with work, and this report proposes that women work more and imposes on fathers a minimum of compulsory and non-transferable paid leave. since everyone has the right to determine how much time they will spend at work and how much with their family, i did not support this report.

mr president, the issue of illegal logging, deforestation and forest degradation is of particular importance for my homeland croatia because almost half of its territory is covered by forests. in recent years, the so-called "forest mafia" has become increasingly active, stealing thousands of cubic feet of timber annually, whether it is firewood or the expensive oak and beech logs that are illegally supplied to the logging industry. the problem is particularly pronounced in private forests where the owners do not live on their property and where property-legal relations are not regulated, but it does not bypass state forests either. thieves are well organized and networked, state forest rangers cannot effectively patrol and prevent theft over such a large area, and the police have a hard time tracking thieves. if we really want to protect forests, the state must manage its own forests more effectively, and private forest owners should be encouraged to form private forest owners' associations and to establish a system of joint supervision that would include a constant exchange of information with the state forestry and police. for countries like croatia, wood is in every sense a strategic resource, and we must not allow anyone to illegally appropriate it and by their predation endanger the future of our forests, their ecosystems and the future of our children.

member of the commission – mr president, i would like to thank all the members for their statements, comments and suggestions, to which i have listened very carefully. i have to say that i agree with many points that have been raised. i will also communicate these to my colleagues, neven mimica, miguel arias and cecilia, with whom i work very closely on deforestation issues. it has already been mentioned that progress is being made even with some timber producers, and in a few weeks’ time we will see the launching of flegt licensing in indonesia. i think this is a major step and one we hope will be followed by ghana next year. at the moment we are discussing vpas with some 15 other countries. so there should be no doubting the commission’s commitment to making flegt work. there were also some interesting points which were made like, for example, mr tomašić, who mentioned the joint surveillance between member states, and the fact that we still have illegal timber coming into europe, and i have to stress again the responsibility of the member states. there is also the fact of the link between deforestation and the agricultural sector, especially the fact that we have to find monoculture and so on, and the socio-economic impact as well. i think many of you also spoke about inadequate implementation and i have to say yes, the commission acknowledges that the absence of an implementation plan to guide strategic management and monitoring has rendered implementation of flegt, and vpas in particular, largely demand-driven. that is why the commission is working towards the development of a multiannual plan to guide activity planning by setting clear targets, indicators, monitoring deadlines and associated budgetary resources. many of the honourable members also mentioned the corruption problem. i totally agree with what they said, and that is why we took a number of precautions, especially in vpas. the scheme developed for vpas has several layers of safeguards and independence. firstly, compliance with legal requirements is checked by private certification companies. secondly, a specific role is provided for civil society to check that audited enterprises and forest operators comply with legal requirements. thirdly, there is an overall systems audit, or periodical evaluation, that is foreseen and that will be carried out at least on an annual basis to check that the system is working properly overall. there were several mentions of dealing with sdgs and climate change, and many of the action plan’s areas of action contribute to addressing several goals of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development, including sdg 8, sdg 12 and sdg 13, which is climate change, sdg 15 which is life on land and sdg 16, which is peaceful and inclusive societies. what the commission intends to do: as indicated in the 7th environmental action plan, the commission remains committed to developing policy proposals to address the deforestation challenge, and to this end the commission is in the process of considering the feasibility of measures to achieve this objective, also as a follow-up to the study on the impact of eu consumption on deforestation. we will continue to ensure adequate resources for the implementation of the action plan, through the development and cooperation instrument, including support for the engagement of civil society, private sector and public administrations. when we talk about resources, as notis marias mentioned, we have not only to monitor and talk about input but, more importantly, i think we written. ‒ i support this report on legal aid for suspects and accused persons and for wanted persons in european arrest warrant proceedings. despite some shortcomings, this is a positive step for the european union and the rule of law. common minimum standards (such as the right to a free lawyer in the issuing country/the country to which the european arrest warrant has been issued) must now be implemented, and we must work to raise the standard and further consolidate the procedural, fundamental and defence rights guaranteed to those who are accused or suspected by our criminal justice system.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a directive of the parliament and of the council on temporary legal aid for suspects or accused persons deprived of their liberty and on legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings because this new directive provides legal aid to all citizens, not just those who can afford it. all member states of the european union have national legal aid systems, but this directive ensures that all citizens have the same minimum rights wherever they are within the eu. this also strengthens mutual trust between member states in the area of criminal justice systems and enhances the proper application of the european arrest warrant.
written. article 6 of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and article 14 of the international covenant on civil and political rights recognize the right to legal aid for persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for it themselves. the purpose of this directive is to ensure the effectiveness of the right of access to a lawyer as established by directive 2013/48/eu of the european parliament and of the council by providing for the financing by member states of the services of a lawyer for suspects or accused persons and for requested persons in surrender proceedings. this directive supports the fundamental rights and principles recognised in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the european convention on human rights, including the prohibition of torture, the right to liberty and security, to an effective remedy, to a fair trial, the presumption of innocence and the right of defence. in order to ensure the effectiveness and quality of legal aid, member states must take the necessary measures to ensure that the standard of legal aid services provided is sufficiently high to protect the right to a fair trial. in any event, this directive applies in full when a suspect or accused person is deprived of liberty, irrespective of the stage of the criminal proceedings. this proposal is a step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states, which is why i supported this report.

written. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is the instrument that primarily addresses the problem of international child abductions following parental separation or divorce, especially when the mother and father are from different countries. in practice, courts in both countries often claim jurisdiction and make different decisions, thus putting children in a position of legal uncertainty. this convention seeks to address this problem at the international level by determining that the courts and applicable laws are those of the child's country of residence. the convention also establishes a system to guarantee the prompt return of abducted children. the convention has been ratified by all eu member states. the eu now has exclusive external competence in this area, as confirmed by the court, but the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations and therefore the eu must give all member states the power to accept the accession of a new member to the convention. in the event of peru's accession to the convention, a council decision is required to enable austria and romania to accept peru's accession thereby allowing the convention between peru and the whole of the european union to enter into force. all other member states have given their consent to peru's accession to the convention. i support this report because the aim of such a convention is to be ratified by as many countries as possible, thereby making it more effective.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of kazakhstan's accession to the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction as the commission, together with civil law experts from the member states, considered it desirable for the convention between the european union and kazakhstan to enter into force. the problems of international child abduction arise when parents from different countries divorce and one parent takes a child to his or her own country without the consent of the other parent. in such cases, most national courts are biased and often the courts in both countries are declared competent. i support the fact that this convention resolves the problem at the international level by declaring the court of the child's country of residence competent and by introducing a system that guarantees the prompt return of abducted children.

written. ‒ international accounting standards (ias) are one of the key components needed for the effective functioning of the internal and capital markets. the use of such instruments should not jeopardise financial stability and should serve the general good, not just the interests of investors, lenders and creditors. the importance and comprehensiveness of these standards require maximum preparation which will not only focus on the desired consequences of their application but will also devote the necessary attention to assessments of other possible impacts on various aspects of the financial system. in this process, the cooperation of the european commission and other bodies involved in these standards, which have already made us aware of the estimates of possible negative impacts of ifrs 9, such as those on long-term investments, is crucial. i consider that the level of involvement of the european parliament in the standard-setting process is not sufficient and i support this resolution which also formally expresses concern about certain shortcomings of the international accounting standards ifrs 9.

written. ‒ food contact materials are an issue that concerns each of the half a billion eu citizens as they come into contact with them on a daily basis. many citizens buy organic food to avoid pesticides, and the contamination potential of chemicals in food packaging can be a thousand times greater. the current directive dates from 2004, and in the meantime, science and toxicology have advanced. i therefore consider it necessary to review existing rules and procedures in order to strengthen the common market and better protect public health. serious consideration should be given to the interaction of compounds and chemicals that may be harmless on their own but can cause a reaction in humans when combined. furthermore, the rules for paper, cardboard, coatings, inks, metals and adhesives should be harmonised. in conclusion, i would like to thank the rapporteur for her efforts and call on the commission to take the steps proposed in the report as soon as possible.
written. ‒ i voted for the implementation report on the food contact materials regulation because i believe that food safety is a very relevant topic. food contact materials (fcms) are widely used in everyday life and when brought into contact with food, some materials, depending on their composition and properties, transfer their constituents to the food. in such cases, the chemicals released by such materials may endanger human health or have a detrimental effect on the composition of the food. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties on the use of the substance in question. however, there is certainly room for progress and further harmonisation as member states may adopt specific measures at national level for those materials, and those measures vary from member state to member state. there are also many materials that are not regulated and that pose a risk to human health. i support this report, but i am aware that action is needed at eu level to bring about an even better and more stringent solution.
written. ‒ the supervision and control measures related to food contact materials (fcms) on the eu market are essential to maintain safety and manage the potential risk of human exposure to hazardous chemicals. consequently, further harmonisation of the rules related to fcms in the areas of risk assessment and enforcement and compliance control is necessary. some institutions, such as the european food safety authority, deal with food contact materials, but their action is limited. the controls that states are required to carry out under the regulation on official controls on food and feed are rarely regular. the control procedures vary across the eu member states and the documentation that accompanies these checks is often unavailable or incomplete. in order to ensure effective supervision of fcms within the eu, it is necessary to fill in the gaps in risk assessment, to follow materials in every part of the supply chain and to ensure compliance and the successful implementation of controls. the existing framework of measures should be adapted in order to better achieve the objectives of preserving and protecting the health of consumers and to improve the efficiency of the existing internal market for food. in view of the forthcoming claims, i supported this report, as i believe that product safety standards in the eu must ensure and protect the health of consumers and facilitate controls in the member states.
written. ‒ i support the resolution on the implementation of the regulation on materials and articles intended to come into contact with food. i believe that we need to introduce common eu-wide measures for most food contact materials because acting in accordance with the requirements of different national rules is neither efficient nor effective in achieving the objectives. it is also important that producers and processors provide complete information and that there is a good level of cooperation between scientific bodies and laboratories in all member states in order to ensure the health of food, but also to enable technological innovation in the future based on clear and uniform rules. in accordance with one of the main objectives of the regulation, namely the protection of human health, the commission should also examine the effects of interaction and multiple exposures to such materials when setting migration limits from materials considered safe for human health. the commission has also identified a number of areas where the union should take action, such as the implementation of the union's policy on the prevention of and control of organised crime, the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, the fight against money laundering and the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, and the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing.
written. ‒ the principle of mutual recognition does not apply to national measures, so that the effective functioning of the internal market and a high level of health protection cannot be guaranteed. i recommend the introduction of harmonised eu standards for the analytical testing of food contact material categories. further measures at eu level would provide an incentive for companies to develop safe fcms that can be recycled and reused, contributing to the eu's efforts to establish a more efficient circular economy. full attention should be paid to the adoption of specific measures for 13 materials that are not yet regulated at eu level. i particularly support further research into nanomaterials, given that their effects on human health have not yet been scientifically established with certainty. nanomaterials should be subject to a procedure for authorisation of use. the ceramic regulation also needs to be revised. i call on the commission to increase the level of funding to efsa in view of the additional work required due to the increased need to carry out risk assessment. the absence of specific measures encourages the emergence of barriers to the internal market, with increased costs often passed on to consumers. member states shall ensure that the necessary staff and equipment are available to carry out uniform, robust and systematic checks and to establish a system of dissuasive penalties in the event of non-compliance.
written. ‒ food comes into contact with a number of materials and articles (fcms) during storage, processing, serving and final consumption. although they should be inert in structure and not affect the quality of food or the health of consumers, some materials behave unexpectedly and transfer their constituents to food. this is primarily the case for endocrine disruptors hormone-disrupting chemicals present in a wide range of commonly used products such as pesticides and biocides, food packaging materials, dishes, etc. they have a significant negative impact on health, causing cancer, fertility problems, obesity, neurobehavioral disorders such as hyperactivity, etc. also, among these chemicals, the most well-known is certainly bisphenol a, to which we are exposed through plastic food packaging, plastic bottles, and baby bottles. i supported the european parliament resolution on the implementation of the regulation on materials in contact with food in order to develop better synergies between the fcms framework regulation and the circular economy in light of the eu's move towards a circular economy, which should include harmonised methods for testing the harmfulness of these materials, banning their use and adopting specific measures for their regulation across the european union.

written. ‒ successful implementation of legislation is a key means of achieving the eu's objectives. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the conditions for the application of the provisions of this directive. although the proper implementation of legislation depends largely on the member states themselves, some factors, such as unrealistic implementation deadlines, prevent the member states from achieving the objectives of certain directives. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the eu acquis in the member states. the monitoring of the application of eu legislation would be facilitated by more systematic reporting and improved access to information for parliament, member states and eu citizens. in addition, member states should be allowed room for manoeuvre in the implementation of directives, in order to ensure their timely application and avoid delayed transposition. the european parliament should have a greater role in monitoring the implementation of eu law, as its participation would allow for the follow-up of individual cases and thus build on the existing knowledge within its relevant committees. in order to allow this, parliament should be given access to information on pending cases and other issues related to the implementation of eu law. i supported this report because i believe that the effective application of eu law is one of the most important factors in strengthening the credibility of the institutions of the european union and in achieving its objectives.
‒ the commission's 32nd annual report on the monitoring of the application of eu law contains information on the actual implementation and practical application of eu law. the majority of infringements in 2014 were in the area of environmental protection, transport and the internal market. the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased over the last five years, which i consider to be a good progress compared to the amount of eu rules in force in the member states. according to the european commission, this reflects the effectiveness of the dialogue with member states in the context of the eu infringement procedure (eu pilot). however, given that parliament still has relatively little access to information on the implementation of these procedures and pending cases, it is difficult to assess to what extent the reduction in formal infringement procedures actually reflects better compliance with eu law by member states rather than compromise solutions between the commission and member states. the european parliament could and should play a structural role in analysing and developing appropriate support for eu law in both acceding and countries with an association agreement with the european union. i supported the report because it points to real problems and i expect that in future reports the commission will also take account of the european parliament's demands just made.
written. ‒ the main responsibility for the correct implementation and application of eu law lies with the member states, but this does not relieve the eu institutions of their duty to respect eu primary law when drafting eu secondary law. the eu pilot aims to bring closer cooperation between the commission and the member states in order to correct violations of eu legislation at an early stage, avoiding the need to initiate formal infringement proceedings. unrealistic deadlines for implementing legislation may result in member states being unable to meet them, thus tacitly granting a delay in application more realistic deadlines for applying regulations and directives are needed. i believe that fines for non-compliance with eu law should be effective, proportionate and dissuasive and should be set taking into account repeated non-compliance and respecting the legal rights of the member states. poor implementation and enforcement play an important role in a series of european crises and create unequal conditions in the single market. parliament should make an additional contribution by sharing its expertise on the legislative process with national parliaments. the commission should also be able to draw up reports, not just resolutions, in response to the annual progress reports drawn up by the commission and to assist in the review of the implementation of legislation by exercising oversight over the commission.

written. ‒ one of the commission's competences includes monitoring the application of eu law. accordingly, it is empowered to initiate proceedings against member states which are in breach of their obligations under the treaty. in order to achieve more effective controls, an eu pilot procedure is envisaged, which aims to reduce the initiation of official infringement procedures through cooperation between the commission and the member state. the 32nd annual monitoring report on enforcement by the commission shows a decrease in the number of formal proceedings attributed by the commission to prior cooperation with member states. however, due to the parliament's incomplete insight into the eu pilot procedure, it cannot be assessed whether this is due to cooperation with member states or member states are less likely to breach their obligations. the commission and parliament have an obligation to cooperate with each other. it is necessary to develop a procedure to allow for better cooperation between the two institutions in order to monitor the application of eu legislation. the commission shall be assisted by the european parliament and the council.
written. ‒ this own-initiative report on the monitoring of the application of eu legislation for 2014 highlights that the number of cases of infringement of legislation has decreased. since parliament has only limited information on the procedure, it is difficult to assess the reasons for the decline in infringements, and in particular whether this is due to the general improvement in the alignment of national legislative systems with those of the european union. however, i believe that in general one of the root causes of the infringements is the unrealistic implementation deadlines imposed on individual member states of the union. member states should certainly be given more time for inquiry and consultation. although i support the parts of the report calling on the commission to take account of the above, i voted in abstention because unfortunately the report does not incorporate amendments calling for respect for the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality in the application of union legislation.

written. ‒ i supported this resolution as i consider that the draft commission implementing decision goes beyond the powers provided for in directive 2001/18/ec and is not in line with its objective of protecting human health and the environment in certain cases where genetically modified organisms are deliberately released into the environment. it is the modifications to bt11 expressing the gene for the cry1ab protein, namely the bt protein (derived from bacillus thuringiensis of the kurstaki sub-species) which provides resistance to the presence of the maize moth (ostrinia nubilalis) and the mediterranean maize moth (sesamia nonagrioides), and to the pat protein which provides tolerance to the ammonium glufosinate herbicides that will not have their expected economic effect. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties on the renewal of the approval of glufosinate, which expires in 2017. i see no reason why approval should be given to seeds that will only be used for one year and that with the use of substances with known adverse health effects.
‒ in 2005, efsa issued an opinion concluding that there are no compatible relatives with which maize could be crossed in nature and that no adverse environmental effects are expected from the cultivation and spread of this species. the spanish competent authorities have informed the commission of the presence of theosinte in spanish maize fields, including a very limited presence in fields of genetically modified maize, and that the available data indicate that theosinte has also been found in france. since theosine populations can become recipients of transgenic dna derived from genetically modified maize mon 810 and thereby produce bt toxin, this allows for a higher survival capacity of maize-theosine hybrids compared to the indigenous plants of theosine. this is a scenario that carries a high risk to farmers and the environment. i consider that this draft commission decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in directive 2001/18/ec. the risk assessment of farming carried out by efsa is not complete and the risk management recommendations made by the commission are not adequate. the draft commission implementing decision is not in accordance with union law as it is incompatible with the objective of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 which is, in accordance with the precautionary principle, to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states concerning the protection of human health and the environment when genetically modified organisms are deliberately released into the environment.

written. ‒ taking into account the draft implementing decision of the european commission on the placing on the market of genetically modified maize bt11 (syn-btø11-1) seed for cultivation, and since the cultivation of genetically modified maize bt11 is prohibited in the territories of certain member states, including croatia, pursuant to article 26c (2) of directive 2001/18/ec, the draft implementing decision of the european commission exceeds its implementing powers as established by directive 2001/18/ec. in addition, the risk assessment of the cultivation by the european food safety authority is incomplete and the commission's draft implementing decision is not sufficiently aligned with the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states protecting human health and the environment in the event of the deliberate introduction of genetically modified organisms for any purpose other than placing on the union market. i therefore support the objection and the european parliament resolution on the commission's draft implementing decision to place genetically modified maize bt11 (syn-btø11-1) seed for cultivation on the market.

madam president, the proposed european union mechanism for democracy and the rule of law and fundamental rights is not in line with the fundamental treaties of the european union, nor with the very principles of the charter of human rights of the european union which it proposes as the legal basis for legislative measures, including sanctions, against member states. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the application of the principle of proportionality. the provisions of the charter of human rights apply to the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the union, subject to the principle of subsidiarity, and to the member states only when they are implementing union law. the charter does not extend the scope of union law beyond the competences of the union, does not create new competences or tasks for the union, and does not alter the competences and tasks as laid down in the treaties. the mechanism proposed in this report is not acceptable as it is not in line with the fundamental treaties of the european union and the charter of human rights of the european union and violates the principle of subsidiarity of sovereign member states.

‒ europe is rich in rivers and canals suitable for the development of the transport sector. inland waterways in large parts of our continent have a strong direct impact on economic activity, but of course we must not overlook their potential for passenger transport either. any policy for developing an area should be based on reliable statistics, and so accurate data on this aspect of inland navigation is needed to boost passenger transport. parliament therefore decided at first reading to extend the scope of the inland waterway freight statistics regulation to passenger transport, and steps have now been agreed to develop a concrete methodology for collecting data and assessing its feasibility. i believe that inland waterway transport must be given a level playing field with the maritime, air and road transport sectors, for which statistics are collected for both goods and passengers. i support today's proposal and hope that the results of its implementation will eventually lead to a stronger development of this form of passenger transport.
written. ‒ parliament considered at first reading that a successful policy to strengthen the role of inland navigation within the transport sector should be based on reliable statistics covering the transport of goods and passengers. the extension of the scope of the existing regulation would put inland waterway transport on an equal footing with the maritime, air and road transport sectors. parliament and the council agreed on this and identified the first steps towards the inclusion of passenger transport statistics in the regulation. the commission will, first, develop a methodology for the collection of statistical data on passenger transport on inland waterways in cooperation with the member states. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and to monitor the implementation of the new rules. the funding of those pilot projects should be supported by the eu budget. parliament and the council agreed to limit the power of the commission to adopt delegated acts. delegated acts should only be adopted to adapt the regulation to changes in labelling and nomenclature at international level and to increase the thresholds. the duration of the delegation shall be limited to five years.
written. ‒ i voted for the report on statistics on inland waterway freight transport, as this is the way to lay the foundations for the development of this type of transport. i support the proposal to adapt the existing definitions and to adapt the scope of data collection and the content of the annexes, and by extending the scope to passenger transport, this type of transport will be placed on an equal footing with other transport sectors. the negotiations between the european parliament and the council have agreed that the commission, in cooperation with the member states, will develop methodologies for the collection of statistical data on passenger transport on inland waterways and launch voluntary pilot studies to examine the feasibility of new ways of collecting data. i consider that this has taken into account the balance between the needs of the users and the reduced increase in the burden at national level.

written. ‒ i voted to refer the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a directive of the parliament and of the council on the legal framework of the union for customs offences and sanctions back to the committee responsible, following the opinion of the alde group and the rapporteur.
written. ‒ the union's legal framework for customs offences and sanctions is particularly important in today's world, where the growth of e-commerce, especially micro-enterprises, requires greater legal certainty to avoid being influenced by the various customs authorities and administrations. although customs rules should already be the same everywhere, when we are faced with the violation of these rules, there is a big difference in the punishment. it is therefore necessary to identify customs duties to which special attention and protection should be given by establishing non-punitive sanctions for possible breaches of those duties. such obligations would be harmonised across the european union and would reduce 'overlap' between individual national enforcement bodies and establish a common platform of rules. this would contribute to a fair and equitable treatment of all economic factors in the european union and at the same time protect the economic interests of the european union. i support this proposal because i believe that harmonising customs offences and, in particular, the sanctions for those offences will contribute to the achievement of justice and the fundamental freedoms of the european union.
written. ‒ the purpose of this directive should be to harmonise the non-punitive sanctions for breaches of customs legislation in order to achieve the most appropriate framework for increasing compliance and reducing the number of infringements. although the customs union is considered one of the foundations of the european union and the backbone of the single market, there is still no integrated approach to the enforcement of customs legislation, including sanctions. this means that the rules are the same, but the sanctions for breaking them are very different. it is clear that without an integrated approach the customs administrations of the member states cannot act as one. the differences create a lack of mutual trust between administrations, which is crucial for the good governance of the customs union. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 concerning the conditions for the authorisation of the use of the term 'authorised economic operator' in the context of the application of this regulation. this is becoming increasingly important with the growth of e-commerce, especially in the case of micro-enterprises and individuals. we also need to prevent the phenomenon of so-called "best-case-scenario jurisdiction". in order to ensure that penalties are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, it is important to leave the customs authorities the possibility to assess the relevant circumstances and, on the basis of that assessment, to decide on the most appropriate sanction. we must abide by the international commitments made in the wto.
written. ‒ the european union can develop a common approach to the enforcement of customs legislation through the interaction and action of customs administrations in an equally effective way as if it were a single administration, since customs legislation is the competence of the european union. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. such differences are the cause of mistrust and insufficient cooperation between administrations which consequently undermine the level playing field for all economic operators in the european union. the commission considers that the conditions for the application of the principle of proportionality are fulfilled. the commission should also be able to take into account the specificities of the member states' customs legislation. i support the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the legal framework of the union for customs offences and sanctions by the committee on the internal market and consumer protection.
written. ‒ this directive allows for the imposition of sanctions for customs infringements by approximating the provisions contained in the laws, regulations and codes of the individual member states of the union. the commission has also proposed to amend the existing rules on the application of the anti-dumping duty on imports of certain footwear with uppers of leather originating in the people's republic of china and taiwan, in order to allow the application of the new rules on the application of the anti-dumping duty on certain footwear with uppers of leather originating in the people's republic of china. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties on the alleged dumping margins. the commission therefore concludes that the measures in force are in line with the principle of the protection of legitimate expectations. on the contrary, the implementation of the same could only lead to problems in practice, in particular related to the lack of flexibility that many member states use on a daily basis in contact with their trading partners. logically, the proposal resulted in the explicit opposition of 15 of the 28 member states of the union in the council. although the original proposal was watered down and modified by requiring only the harmonisation of the maximum level of sanctions, i voted against because i am always against such attempts by the commission which undermine both of the fundamental principles on which the european union is founded.

written. ‒ democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights are key principles, enshrined in the treaty articles themselves and in the eu membership criteria. the european commission has the right to intervene to ensure the compliance of national legislation with eu law, and member states do not contest the fact that the eu treaties oblige them to ensure compliance. however, when it comes to implementing the treaty's obligations on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, the european commission's interventions are cautious, arbitrary and met with resistance or complete rejection by member states. an additional problem is that the eu institutions themselves have sometimes failed to respect the key principles of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. this is why it was necessary to create an integrated mechanism for systematic, impartial and full monitoring of all member states and institutions. it is time to create the right conditions to protect the fundamental european values in practice. i consider the adoption of the eu pact for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the form of an interinstitutional agreement to be an important step. the new single framework should be objective, evidence-based and apply equally and fairly to all member states and include a preventive and corrective dimension. it will provide for an integrated audit mechanism applicable to all member states as well as to the three main eu institutions.

written. trans-fatty acids are naturally found in food obtained from mammals, in some plants, and in human breast milk. however, most of the trans fatty acids consumed are industrially produced. thus, intake of trans-fatty acids is also mainly associated with consumption of industrial food products. there is evidence of health risks associated with the consumption of trans fatty acids and the cause of obesity in humans. i believe that the european institutions should take certain measures to protect the health of european citizens, which primarily relates to better information through the education system. i also believe that a policy aimed at limiting the proportion of trans fatty acids in food products is necessary. i see this motion for a resolution as a step towards more effective information on the harmful effects of the consumption of industrial trans-fatty acids and as the beginning of the development of a strategy to limit their use. i am convinced that a decision on trans-fatty acids at eu level would have a positive impact on public health.
