written. ‒ the european order for payment is an optional procedure which can be used as an alternative to domestic orders for payment in cross-border court cases and was introduced to enable the quick and cheap recovery of amounts arising from secured and maturing debts of a fixed amount which have not been contested by the defendant. the european order for payment is necessary for the functioning of the internal market. the liquidity shortfall is caused by late payments, which pose a serious threat to smes, especially as a large number of jobs are lost. the procedure allows creditors to obtain an order for the recovery of uncontested civil and commercial claims in a simple manner. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the conditions for the participation of third countries in union programmes in the field of scientific and technical research and technological development, in particular in the framework of the european research area. the european parliament welcomed the successful functioning of the european order for payment procedure in all member states so far, in order to simplify and accelerate the procedure for the cross-border recognition and enforcement of credit claims in the european union. since i agree with everything that was written in the report, i supported it.
written. i support the assessment of the application of regulation (ec) no 1896/2006 of the european parliament and of the council for the creation of a european payment order. the purpose of the european order for payment procedure is to facilitate the recovery of amounts in cross-border procedures. the procedure is optional, meaning that it is available in cross-border cases as an alternative to various equivalent national procedures. in other words, this procedure allows creditors to obtain an order for the recovery of uncontested civil and commercial claims in a simple manner. the request for a procedure may be sent by post, and often by electronic means, without the assistance of a lawyer, and the order shall be enforceable in other member states without the need for any further formalities. it also allows the free movement of european payment orders that are recognised and executed in all eu countries. the european order for payment applies to all eu countries except denmark. the european order for payment procedure applies to all civil and commercial matters where at least one of the parties resides in an eu country other than the one in which the application for the order is made.
written. ‒ the existing procedure allows for a quick and cheap recovery of amounts, but it still operates below the limits of its full potential, which is necessary for the internal market to function even more successfully. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties. our main objective is to simplify and speed up the process of cross-border recognition and enforcement of creditors' rights in the eu. the long-awaited commission report does not contain an extended impact assessment for each member state and does not contain updated information on the functioning and application of the european order for payment procedure. i call for an extended and updated impact assessment, with member states providing the commission with accurate and comprehensive data. we need to eliminate differences in the application of the procedure between member states, otherwise european citizens cannot fully exercise their rights at cross-border level, which weakens trust in eu legislation. it is necessary to allow applicants to submit applications in additional languages, without which payment delays are often a key cause of illiquidity and threaten the survival of businesses and the loss of many jobs. in any event, the 30-day time limit laid down by the regulations should be respected. we also need to enable our citizens to submit applications electronically in the future, and i therefore welcome the work on the development of the e-codex system.

in writing. ‒ i support the motion for a resolution on the application of the european order for payment procedure. the dogmatic rationale for introducing the payment order institution is to enable the collection of due claims to be made more simply and efficiently. since the european union is a single market, it is necessary to codify effectively and then apply adequate legal mechanisms to facilitate the functioning of the union system. since bureaucratic obstacles to the recovery of claims still exist to a certain extent, it is necessary to provide for and regulate a procedure that will simplify the recovery of uncontested civil and commercial claims. i certainly support the initiative of enforcement of an order in a member state which does not belong to it by territorial jurisdiction, especially since in this case it will not be necessary to activate the legal services which generate additional costs for citizens.
written. ‒ the purpose of the european payment order is to facilitate the recovery of money in cross-border disputes. the procedure allows creditors to recover undisputed civil and commercial claims more easily. the proposal significantly reduces the bureaucratic burden, as it also allows the application of the above in writing, i.e. by electronic mail, and does not require the involvement of a lawyer or the completion of other formalities. the order shall be issued automatically, and only on the basis of a prior application, and the debtor shall have the right to make representations within 30 days. when taking into account the cost of cross-border procedures, and the exceptional length of procedures in certain member states of the union, the settlement of procedures by means of a european order for payment is clearly a much cheaper and faster solution. that's why i voted yes.

mr. president, i congratulate the rapporteurs and the commissioners on a great job and a good report. we want to modernise the railway sector, make it innovative, encourage the use of new technologies and new business models. the aim, of course, is to provide all our citizens with the safest, best quality and cheapest rail services possible, all of which is brought about by the opening of markets and increased competition. however, we must take into account the great differences in the development of the railway infrastructure which is the basis for the development of transport and management services. for example, in croatia we are facing major investments in rail infrastructure, and the services market could not have developed without it. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the aid granted to the railway undertakings in croatia is compatible with the internal market. therefore, i call on the european commission and expect that croatia will be provided with specific business models that will accelerate investments in railway infrastructure, as well as the development of service companies so that the empowered can participate on an equal footing in this new model and package for railway services.
mr president, too many initiatives have sprung up in this house to establish costly universal governance models that unnecessarily undermine european diversity and seek to replace existing national models. this report does the exact opposite and i must commend it. the rapporteur acknowledges the diversity of port and port services management models within the european union and rejects the establishment of a single system. if something works well, it doesn't need to be fixed. i also welcome the insistence on competition, but i must express my concern about the imposition of minimum requirements for the provision of port services. of course, we aim to provide services by competent and reliable companies, but we must be careful that the minimum requirements are not too strict, because we will leave room only for the largest companies. in this way we would create an oligopoly and achieve the opposite of the effects that the rapporteur and all of us want.

mr president, commissioners, the commission's proposals on clean energy for all europeans reflect the fact that the clean energy transition is a growth sector of the future and an opportunity for smart investors. this package, which will mobilise public and private investment of eur 177 billion per year by 2021, can increase gross national income by up to 1% and create 900 000 new jobs over the next 10 years. europe imports energy worth €1 billion a day. investing in energy efficiency reduces the need for energy production. by investing in it, we are investing in the european economy, we are investing in our homes, we are investing in our manufacturing, in our small entrepreneurs who are renovating our homes. it's better to invest a billion euros a day in our economy than to pay for energy from imports. the potential of biomass and biofuels based on the sustainable management of these resources should also be better exploited. europe and croatia are doing well in this.
written. energy efficiency, the use of renewable energy sources and the involvement of consumers in production are the cornerstones of the new energy package. this new package encourages innovative solutions, new technologies and better connections between different sectors. we are the world's first circular economy, and the new energy package is an extra incentive to keep it that way. however, these objectives are not matched by sufficient regulatory flexibility or the speed of investment in innovative solutions. we still have major problems with pollutants throughout europe that threaten human health and we should not passively watch these examples. to talk about a new package and not to deal with pollution cases like the one in slavonski brod caused by production in bosanski brod is to be inconsistent. according to the european environment agency, some pollutants transform into airborne particles that can affect countries far from the source of the pollution. the published graphs show that 63% of all air pollution in the netherlands comes from outside its borders. in the case of the czech republic, this percentage is around 70%, and the pollution emitted by the czech republic is as high as 80%. given that pollution knows no borders, it is essential to develop awareness of the need for cross-border cooperation and the implementation of joint projects with non-eu countries.

written. ‒ deep-sea fishing accounts for about 1% of landings from the north-east atlantic, and some fishing communities are economically dependent on deep-sea fishing. over time, it has become clear that the original rules for deep-sea fisheries are not sufficiently restrictive and can no longer ensure the sustainable management of the stocks. in addition, they do not address the problem of significant adverse impacts on sensitive marine ecosystems. i therefore voted in favour of this report which brings about significant improvements in the rules on deep-sea fishing in the north-east atlantic. this regulation was adopted after four years of political negotiations and the new rules should apply by the end of 2016. some of these include a ban on fishing with trawls below 800 metres, a rule that vessels can only fish in areas where they have previously fished to prevent further damage, an obligation for vessels to report encounters with sensitive marine ecosystems at depths greater than 400 metres and then move to another fishing area, more rigorous control measures to ensure that everyone follows the same rules, and to ensure data collection, scientific observers will have to board 20% of vessels fishing in eu waters and those bordering the eu.

madam president, commissioner, price volatility in agricultural product markets is one of the causes of farmers' insecurity and affects their ability to produce and create jobs. the commission should also be able to assess the impact of the measures on the environment and the environment protection of the union's forests, in particular by assessing the impact of the measures on the environment and the environment. the income that should guarantee them a decent life is disappearing. this discourages their investment in modernisation, innovation, prevents young farmers from entering the labour market and generational renewal of rural areas. family farms are the most vulnerable link in the food supply chain. it is for this reason that legislation at european level should tackle unfair trading practices and provide a legal framework for the implementation of measures such as collective bargaining for longer contract terms, stable prices for agricultural products, reasonable payment periods and other conditions linked to production, aimed at a balanced distribution of production risks throughout the food supply chain.
madam president, the european council will be discussing youth unemployment, a problem that is very troubling to my homeland, croatia. since becoming an mep, i have stressed that insisting on mobility might lead to better statistics at eu level, but it opens up a whole host of other big problems. today young people from croatia easily go to other eu member states for work. the richer members are getting skilled workers, and croatia is seeing a sharp drop in unemployment. politicians on both sides are happy to rub their hands together. some because they import good workers who integrate quickly and easily into society, and others because they boast nice statistics. but few seem to understand that croatia and other members in a similar situation will soon be facing dire economic and social problems that more developed members will have to overcome. youth unemployment should be addressed at the level of each member state individually, rather than by bringing together people from less developed to richer member states.

written. ‒ the agreement on mutual access to fishing in the skagerrak and kattegat between denmark, norway and sweden entered into force in 1967. that agreement, supplemented by the bilateral fisheries agreement between the european union and norway of 1980, allowed the three states to borrow access to fisheries up to four nautical miles from their baselines in the skagerrak and kattegat. this agreement further supports the historical fishing rights in that area and will be useful for the implementation of the reformed common fisheries policy in the kattegat and skagerrak. having regard to the recommendation of the committee on fisheries, parliament gave its consent to the conclusion of this agreement. that's why i endorsed this report.
written. ‒ the eu's common fisheries policy provides for a system of management of fish stocks in waters that upholds the historical rights of fishermen. the commission has therefore entered into formal negotiations with norway on behalf of the eu with a view to establishing a replacement agreement on mutual access to fishing in the skagerrak and kattegat between denmark, norway and sweden. the new agreement is consistent with the un convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 un fish stocks agreement and subsequent related provisions in other agreements. it guarantees vessels from denmark, norway and sweden continued exclusive mutual access to waters more than four nautical miles from their baselines and provides those two member states and norway with continued mutual access to each other's waters in the skagerrak and kattegat. at the same time, it shall ensure that reasonable measures are taken to conserve and manage fisheries in the area. the fishing tradition predates the formation of states and the recognition of territorial waters and the much later creation of exclusive economic zones. respect for historical fishing rights is of the utmost importance and i therefore supported this resolution giving my assent to the council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on reciprocal access to fishing in the skagerrak for vessels flying the flag of denmark, norway and sweden.
written. ‒ traditionally, fishermen do not fish in certain waters, but catch certain species in waters where these species can be found. the kattegat and skagerrak are typical examples and the older traditions of territorial waters recognition and the principle that fishermen from denmark, sweden and norway should enjoy a historical right to fish in that area should be protected. the previously existing tripartite agreement of 1966, supplemented by the bilateral fisheries agreement between the european union and norway of 1980, allowed those states to borrow access to fisheries within four nautical miles of their baselines in the skagerrak and kattegat. in view of recent developments in international law, norway considered that the existing agreement was not in conformity with the provisions of the law of the sea and in july 2009 formally announced its wish to terminate the agreement it ceased to be valid on 7 august 2012. norway has since entered into formal negotiations with the commission with a view to establishing a replacement agreement consistent with the un convention on the law of the sea, which was subsequently signed on 15 january 2015. it provides for continued mutual access by those states to each other's waters in the skagerrak and kattegat and provides for prudent conservation and management measures for fisheries in that area.

written. ‒ the agreement on mutual access to fishing in the skagerrak and kattegat between denmark, norway and sweden grants those states exclusive mutual access to waters more than four nautical miles from their baselines, while ensuring sound conservation and management measures for fisheries in that area. traditionally, fishermen do not fish in specific waters: they hunt for specific stocks or species and fish in waters where those stocks or species can be found. this tradition is older than the formation of states and the recognition of territorial waters, and the kattegat and skagerrak are typical examples of this. the fact that two of those states are eu member states does not change the principle that fishermen from all three states should enjoy the historical right to fish in the skagerrak and kattegat. it is of the utmost importance that these historic fishing rights are respected. i therefore support this report as this agreement further supports the historical fishing rights in that area and will be useful for the implementation of the reformed common fisheries policy in the kattegat and skagerrak.
written. ‒ the agreement on mutual access to fishing in the skagerrak and kattegat regulates the rules for the danish, norwegian and swedish flagged prawns and has been in force since 1967. following the accession of denmark and sweden to the european union, it was supplemented by a bilateral fisheries agreement between the european union and norway, but now needs to be aligned with the principles of normal coastal state jurisdiction within the meaning of the un convention on the law of the sea and not to correspond to modern conservation and management principles. as in the previous agreement, vessels from denmark, norway and sweden are guaranteed exclusive mutual access to waters more than four nautical miles from their baselines and are provided with sound conservation and management measures for fisheries in that area. the agreement also provides for control measures in accordance with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of the coastal state. since i believe that this is a way of upholding the historical fishing rights of those countries in the kattegat and skagerrak, i have supported this agreement.

written. ‒ under regulation 1192/69 on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings, which the commission proposes to repeal, member states are allowed to reimburse those undertakings for the payment of obligations which do not apply to carriers in other modes of transport. these commitments may relate to special payments in the event of accidents at work, pensions for railway workers or payment of the cost of railway and road facilities. the report also notes that the current text of the regulation is discriminatory in that it provides for the possibility of compensation for only 40 companies listed in the annexes to the regulation. the report suggests to follow the commission's proposal to repeal the regulation, with the exception of the provisions applying to the normalisation of accounts for category iv cases, which continue to apply until 31 december 2017. this will give member states time to adapt their national legislation regarding the reimbursement of costs associated with certain railway and road infrastructure. given that the council's position at first reading is in line with the agreement reached during the interinstitutional negotiations, i did not support the proposal to reject the council's position.
written. ‒ the standardisation of railway accounts proposed by the commission to be abolished allows railway undertakings and member states to compensate for the payment of obligations not applicable to carriers in other modes of transport. the commission notes that the compensation granted to the railway undertaking for the provision of services to the public is not limited to the costs of the infrastructure and the costs of the infrastructure manager. the types of remuneration for such obligations are divided into 15 categories governing the specific scope and principles of calculation. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the compensation granted to the railway undertakings for the provision of the services provided by the railway undertakings in question is compatible with the internal market. however, following several railway packages that transformed the railway sector, the regulation is no longer in line with the existing legal environment and it implements discrimination between those railway undertakings included in the list and those subsequently added to the list. this is to level the playing field for all railway administrations.
written. ‒ regulation 1192/69 is no longer compatible with the existing legal environment, since it was adopted at a time when rail transport in europe was developing mainly within national borders under the management of integrated undertakings. in the meantime, we have liberalised the railway market in europe and now the transformed railway sector is unfortunately subject to discrimination. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the compensation granted to the railway undertakings for the non-payment of the charges for the services provided by the railway undertakings is compatible with the internal market. however, the regulation contains a list of railway undertakings which were formerly state-owned and the possibility of compensation is provided for only for the 40 undertakings mentioned. therefore, the maintenance of the regulation in force is only possible if the list of railway undertakings is regularly updated. however, a transitional period with regard to the payment of railway infrastructure charges is necessary as some member states still use the regulation as the basis for charges and will need time to amend their national legislation and administrative provisions. i call on all member states to continue to transpose the measures of directive 2012/34/eu, avoiding unnecessary delays.

written. ‒ caring for plant health is one of the main foundations for the development of sustainable and competitive agriculture, ensuring healthy and quality food, and protecting the environment in general. the progress of plant health also affects the stable and secure food supply of the national population and the introduction into the republic of croatia of plants and plant products infected with certain harmful organisms is prohibited. recently, we have witnessed the emergence of a dangerous disease that destroys olives, caused by the bacterium xylella fastidiosa (wells et al.), which originates from the americas. the deadly bacterium introduced into the european agro-ecosystem, destroying olive groves, is transmitted by insect vectors, and its emergence and domestication on the salento peninsula in italy represent a phytosanitary risk of the highest degree also for olive growing in the republic of croatia. the eu should identify the phytosanitary risks posed by any species, strain or biotype of pathogenic, animal or plant parasite harmful to plants or plant products and measures to mitigate those risks to an acceptable level. the old council directive 2000/29/ec does not provide the right answers to the risks of diseases such as black rot and bacterial carcinoma of citrus fruit. i therefore supported the eu resolution requesting an amendment to annex i.v to council directive 2000/29/ec on protective measures against the introduction into the community of organisms harmful to plants or plant products and against their spread within the community.
written. ‒ the draft commission implementing directive is not in accordance with union law as it is not compatible with the objective of regulation (eu) 2016/2031 to identify the phytosanitary risks posed by any harmful organism and the measures to mitigate those risks to an acceptable level. the commission was therefore asked to amend its draft implementing directive. the phytosanitary risk is particularly high in the warmer parts of europe. although most citrus imports for processing are destined for regions less susceptible to infected pests coming from outside europe, there is a risk that pests from northern europe could be transferred to warmer areas and thus infect citrus plants. the outbreak of xyllela fastidiosa in italy and the import of invasive alien species into europe demonstrate the need to ensure that all imports of plants or plant products are free from harmful organisms. one infected plant can destroy an entire sector or the economy of an entire region.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, but this explanation of vote is a criticism of the existing system of evaluating the work of meps in the european parliament solely on the basis of the statistical number of parliamentary activities promoted in croatia, which does not actually reflect the actual quality and quantity of work, efficiency and above all the success of the parliamentary activity.
written. ‒ the resolution deals with the introduction of safeguard measures against the introduction of organisms harmful to plants or plant products and their spread within the community. the introduction of safeguard measures should take place as soon as the resolution enters into force. the european parliament considers that the commission proposal is not consistent with union law and is not compatible with resolution (eu) 2016/2031. therefore, calls on the commission to modify and adapt the proposal through the three modifications presented in the resolution to be forwarded to the council and the commission and to the governments and parliaments of the member states. i support this resolution because i believe that food and production need to be better protected.
written. ‒ i support the motion for a resolution on the objection under rule 106 of the rules of procedure: safeguards against the introduction into the community of organisms harmful to plants or plant products and against their spread within the community having regard to articles 11 and 13 of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers. the draft implementing directive is not in line with the objectives of regulation 2016/2031. the draft should be amended to introduce a clause requiring that fruit from third countries must have a phytosanitary certificate and a statement that the area of production of the fruit has been treated appropriately. the following additional declaration is required to be attached: the area of production of the specified fruits has been adequately treated against phyllosticte citricarpe and the farming methods have been implemented at the appropriate time since the beginning of the last cycle of vegetation.
in writing. – i support this report because thalidomide survivors should be formally recognised in all member states concerned and finally be given adequate and fair compensation from the special health fund of the german contergan stiftung.
written. i voted for the motion for a resolution in support of the victims of thalidomide because i believe that such a mistake and playing with human lives must never be repeated. in the 1950s and '60s, the sedative thalidomide was given to pregnant women for morning sickness as a completely safe and proven drug, and then unexpected long-term effects occurred. more than 10,000 were born with severe physical defects, most often deformed arms and legs or without limbs. blindness, deafness, heart problems and brain damage in children are also side effects of taking thalidomide during pregnancy. this motion for a resolution, for which i voted, supports in every way the victims of thalidomide and calls on the commission and the member states to work together and to accelerate measures and activities to give formal recognition and compensation to those victims.
written. ‒ thalidomide was developed in 1960 and is approved as a safe drug for the prevention of morning sickness, headaches, insomnia, and colds in pregnant women. yet, taking this drug has had tragic consequences for many families, resulting in the birth of children with severe malformations. the resolution stresses the need to acknowledge this problem in order to ensure fair compensation for the victims. i supported this resolution.
written. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on support for survivors of thalidomide. the resolution takes into account that the eu marked 50 years since the adoption of the first pharmaceutical regulations in europe to protect its citizens in september 2015. i recall that in may 2015, a press conference was held in brussels, with the support of all political groups, to highlight the unmet health needs of thalidomide victims. in the late 1950's and early 1960's, thalidomide was marketed to pregnant women as a cure for morning sickness, headaches, cough, insomnia, and colds, and its use caused the death and deformity of thousands of children in many european countries. even after the drug was withdrawn from the market, the authorities had a hard time dealing with the situation. it was difficult for them to explain the effects of the drug, to determine the number of people affected and to ban it, and at that time there was no legal framework for banning the drugs. the estimated number of european citizens currently living who have been victims of the german company gruenenthal and its drug is about 4,000, with the highest number in germany at about 2,700. finally, i think that the progress of the current european pharmaceutical regulation, which is firmly based on the precautionary principle and aims to meet high standards of quality and user safety, should be welcomed.
written. ‒ i support the movement resolution on support for victims of thalidomide. i believe that the recently published reports from the institutes in germany and the united kingdom express the need for greater support for the victims of thalidomide. thalidomide was used in the 1950's and 1960's to treat headaches, coughs, and insomnia. however, the shortcomings of the research carried out and the harmful effects of the use of thalidomide were only subsequently identified. i believe that the member states of the european union must submit coordinated measures to formally recognise and implement compensation for victims of thalidomide use. although the number of victims is not evenly distributed across all member states, there is a need to identify the problem at the institutional level of the european union and to respond to it adequately.
written. - thalidomide is a drug that was used about 50 years ago on thousands of women to relieve the symptoms of morning sickness. the drug was a product of the german pharmaceutical company grünenthal and was issued from 1957 to 1961, when it was finally withdrawn after it was found to cause certain deformities in children whose mothers took it during pregnancy. the use of thalidomide has caused the deaths of 2,000 children, and more than 10,000 people are living with severe disabilities today. what is especially sad is the fact that the company that made the drug only apologized to its victims and their families in 2012, but did not admit to the mistake. the thalidomide case was one of the main reasons for the establishment of eu pharmaceutical legislation, which led to a strengthening of the regulatory environment for the development of medical devices. i hereby call on the commission to create a framework protocol under which all european citizens affected by this pharmaceutical disaster will receive equal financial compensation and to establish a community of aid and support for all victims. the minimum that should have been done long ago is for grünenthal to admit its mistake and pay appropriate compensation to all the victims. that is what we all have to stand for here, and that is why i supported this report.

written. ‒ the paediatric medicines regulation has helped to improve the overall situation and has led to concrete benefits in a number of paediatric diseases, but there has been insufficient progress in a number of areas, in particular in paediatric oncology and neonatology. it is therefore urgently necessary to assess how different types of funding can best be used to stimulate and accelerate the development of medicines to treat those cancers that occur in newborns and children. the early implementation of paediatric trial plans, early scientific and regulatory dialogue and cooperation with the european medicines agency with pharmaceutical companies allow for the improvement of the global development of paediatrics, which is why i supported this motion for a resolution.
written. ‒ childhood cancers remain the leading cause of death in children aged one year and over. every year in europe, 6,000 young people die of cancer. the current regulatory approach is not satisfactory for diseases specific to paediatric age and less than 10% of children with incurable and potentially fatal relapses have access to new, experimental medicines in clinical trials. early implementation of paediatric trial plans, early scientific and regulatory dialogue and cooperation with the european medicines agency (ema) and pharmaceutical companies are enabling the improvement of the global development of paediatrics. in line with the provisions of the third eu health programme (2014-2020), i underline the commitment to improve resources and expertise for patients with rare diseases. i also stress the importance of cross-border trials in the investigation of many paediatric and rare diseases and therefore welcome regulation (eu) no 536/2014 of the european parliament and of the council on clinical trials of medicinal products for human use, which will facilitate the conduct of such trials, and call on the ema to secure the infrastructure necessary for its application as soon as possible. i call on the commission to start working urgently on possible regulatory changes that could improve the current situation.
‒ the commission published its first report on the paediatric medicines regulation in 2013, stating that while there is promising progress in a number of areas, more time will be needed to thoroughly assess the impact of the regulation on paediatric medicines development. the regulation requires the commission to publish a second report in 2017. the purpose of this resolution is to seek clarification from the european commission on the progress of the report and to highlight areas and issues where the commission should consider amending the regulation. many cancers affecting children do not occur in adults, and the industry for such cancers, as well as for other diseases that occur only in children, has limited financial incentives to develop specific medicines for paediatric use. many children suffering from rare childhood diseases do not have access to targeted paediatric medicines. in many areas of pediatric medicine, there is a lack of the necessary innovation in the development of new medicines. the regulation has helped to improve the general situation and progress has been made in a number of paediatric diseases, but insufficient progress has been made in a number of areas, in particular paediatric oncology and neonatology. we need to encourage innovation in paediatric drug development to ensure that in the future all children are treated with medicines that are effective and safe and developed specifically for use in children.

on behalf of the alde club. mr. president, we know how it went. there were lines that stood for hours at our border crossings. the trucks have been waiting for hours. rows that were miles long. i regret that there are not some colleagues here who are talking about how the unity within the european union should be broken and how this union should be destroyed. i am sorry that they are not here and that they do not hear and remember how we lived and how it was between our member states, but that is just a political message. i want to make it clear that what these new proposals are proposing to us here is something that will really, i hope, help us. the intention and goals to modernise the customs code in a way that uses digital technology is something that was certainly expected to come on the agenda and that we would have a chance to do business in a more uniform way. the fact that businesses will have greater legal certainty, and that there will be simplification of procedures and the various rules we have, is something that the business world of the european union rightly expects. we also expect that there will be appropriate solutions for e-commerce because it is very important. we know that e-commerce is increasingly present between member states and that eu citizens are increasingly trading in this way. in conclusion, i would like to wish all of you, especially you, mr president, a merry christmas and a happy new year.
mr president, commissioner, the new customs code brings about a concentration of customs regulations, simplification of procedures, which of course means speeding up the procedure. it defines the data needed to carry out this process and ultimately, because of all this, because of the leveling and simplification, acceleration leads to the simplification of doing business in general which will of course also lead to an increase in the competitiveness of the european economy, and all of this is of course part of the european strategy for growth and employment. that's why this is an important topic. the timing of this issue is timely because the customs code came into force this year and its implementation should be monitored very closely. i therefore thank and congratulate my colleagues on the committee on the internal market and consumer protection for proposing this item on the agenda. on the other hand, it is very important that this whole process of introducing this code is monitored and computerized. that's why it's such a long transition period in a way. i would like to congratulate the commission representative in particular on the fact that he also referred to electronic commerce as a very important segment, in which the implementation of this code will of course also help. finally, thank you. merry christmas and a happy new year.
